products.name: subscription
products.description: This association product represents the subscription contract between client_profile and service_package. It captures the commercial terms, pricing, and lifecycle status of each client's subscription to a specific service package. Each record links one client to one service package with subscription-specific attributes including pricing overrides, discount terms, renewal status, and usage tracking that exist only in the context of this subscription relationship. This is the SSOT for all active and historical client-package subscription relationships enabling recurring revenue management, renewal forecasting, and cross-sell analytics.. Existence Justification: In legal services, clients routinely subscribe to multiple service packages simultaneously (e.g., a corporate client may have an ongoing compliance retainer, an IP portfolio management package, and a regulatory advisory package). Conversely, each service package is sold to multiple clients with client-specific pricing, discount terms, renewal cycles, and usage patterns. The subscription relationship is actively managed by relationship partners who negotiate pricing, track renewals, monitor usage, and identify cross-sell opportunities.

attributes.name: subscription_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for this client-package subscription record. Primary key.

attributes.name: package_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the service package record. Identifies which service package the client has subscribed to.

attributes.name: profile_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the client profile record. Identifies which client holds this subscription.

attributes.name: responsible_partner_timekeeper_id
attributes.description: Reference to the partner (timekeeper) responsible for managing this specific subscription relationship, including renewals, pricing negotiations, and service delivery oversight. May differ from the client's overall relationship partner when specialized practice area partners manage specific package subscriptions.

attributes.name: auto_renew_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this subscription automatically renews at the end of the subscription term without requiring explicit client approval. True enables automatic renewal; False requires manual renewal negotiation. Impacts revenue forecasting and client engagement workflows.

attributes.name: billing_frequency
attributes.description: Frequency at which the client is billed for this service package subscription. Determines invoice generation schedule and revenue recognition pattern. May differ from standard package terms based on client-specific agreements.

attributes.name: contract_reference_number
attributes.description: External reference number or identifier for the legal contract or engagement letter governing this service package subscription. Links to physical or electronic contract documents in the document management system for audit and compliance purposes.

attributes.name: created_date
attributes.description: Timestamp when this subscription record was created in the system. Used for audit trail and subscription lifecycle tracking.

attributes.name: discount_applied
attributes.description: Percentage discount applied to the base package price for this client subscription. Captures negotiated discounts, promotional offers, or relationship-based pricing adjustments. Used to calculate package_price from base price and for discount analysis.

attributes.name: end_date
attributes.description: Date when this client's subscription to the service package expires or was terminated. Null indicates an open-ended or currently active subscription. Used for renewal forecasting and revenue recognition cutoff.

attributes.name: last_modified_date
attributes.description: Timestamp when this subscription record was last updated. Tracks changes to pricing, renewal status, or other subscription terms for audit and change management purposes.

attributes.name: package_price
attributes.description: Actual price charged to this specific client for this service package subscription. May differ from the base_price_amount in service_package due to client-specific negotiations, volume discounts, or relationship tier adjustments. Represents the contracted recurring amount.

attributes.name: renewal_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the subscription renewal process. Active indicates ongoing subscription; Pending Renewal indicates approaching expiration requiring client decision; Renewed indicates successful renewal executed; Cancelled indicates client-initiated termination; Expired indicates lapsed without renewal; On Hold indicates temporary suspension. Critical for revenue forecasting and client retention workflows.

attributes.name: start_date
attributes.description: Date when this client's subscription to the service package became active. Marks the beginning of the subscription term and triggers billing cycle initiation.

attributes.name: usage_count
attributes.description: Number of times services within this package subscription have been utilized or invoked by the client. Tracks consumption for usage-based billing models, capacity planning, and value realization analysis. Incremented when matters are opened under this package or when package services are delivered.

products.name: document_access
products.description: This association product represents the access grant between contact and legal_document. It captures the sharing, permission, and access control relationship when legal documents are shared with client contacts through client portals or matter management systems. Each record links one contact to one legal_document with attributes that exist only in the context of this access relationship, including who shared it, when access was granted, permission levels, and expiration dates.. Existence Justification: In legal practice, document sharing and access control is a core operational process managed through client portals and document management systems. A single legal document (contract, brief, disclosure) is routinely shared with multiple client contacts (in-house counsel, compliance officers, business stakeholders, signatories) with different permission levels and access windows. Conversely, each contact accesses many documents across multiple matters over time. The firm actively manages these access grants—creating them when documents are shared, tracking who accessed what and when, setting expiration dates for sensitive documents, and revoking access when matters close or contacts leave client organizations.

products.name: kyc_document_verification
products.description: This association product represents the verification relationship between KYC reviews and supporting legal documents. It captures which documents satisfy which KYC requirements, the verification status of each document within the context of a specific KYC review, verification dates, expiry tracking, and the reviewer responsible. Each record links one KYC dossier to one supporting document with attributes that exist only in the context of this compliance verification relationship.. Existence Justification: In legal practice, a single KYC review dossier requires multiple supporting documents (passport, utility bill, incorporation certificate, beneficial ownership register, financial statements), and a single document (such as audited financials or a corporate registry extract) can legitimately support multiple KYC reviews across related entities (parent/subsidiary relationships) or periodic renewals for the same client. Compliance teams actively manage which documents satisfy which KYC requirements, track verification status per document-per-review, and monitor expiry dates for periodic re-verification.

products.name: matter_risk
products.description: Matter-level operational risk register capturing identified risks specific to the conduct and outcome of an individual matter, distinct from enterprise-level risk records owned by the risk domain. Records risk category (professional indemnity exposure, adverse litigation outcome, regulatory sanction, client credit/collection, data breach, LPP waiver, conflict escalation, scope creep), risk description, likelihood rating, impact rating, inherent risk score, residual risk score, mitigation action, risk owner (timekeeper), identified date, next review date, and risk status (open, mitigated, accepted, escalated, closed). Supports the firms professional indemnity insurance reporting, matter-level risk dashboards, and partner risk review meetings. The enterprise risk domain owns firm-wide risk aggregation and risk appetite frameworks.

products.name: assignment
products.description: This association product represents the Assignment between matter and timekeeper. It captures the staffing relationship where timekeepers are assigned to legal matters in specific roles (responsible attorney, supervising partner, billing attorney, associate, paralegal, etc.) with role-specific billing rates, time allocation budgets, and assignment lifecycle tracking. Each record links one matter to one timekeeper with attributes that exist only in the context of this specific assignment, enabling matter staffing management, resource allocation, billing rate overrides, and workload tracking across the firm.. Existence Justification: In legal practice, matters routinely require multiple timekeepers working in different roles (responsible attorney, supervising partner, associates, paralegals, legal assistants), and timekeepers work on multiple matters concurrently. The matter product already contains four separate FK attributes pointing to timekeeper for specific roles (attorney_profile_id, supervising_partner_attorney_profile_id, originating_attorney_attorney_profile_id, billing_attorney_attorney_profile_id), which is a classic anti-pattern indicating that a proper M:N association is needed. The detection reasoning explicitly states this is already modeled via matter_team and matter_assignment junction tables, confirming the business recognizes this as an operational M:N relationship.

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the legal matter to which the timekeeper is assigned

attributes.description: Percentage of the timekeeper's total capacity allocated to this matter (e.g., 25.00 means 25% of their time). Used for resource planning, workload balancing, and capacity management across the firm.

attributes.name: assignment_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of this assignment. ACTIVE assignments allow time entry and billing. PLANNED assignments are future staffing. ON_HOLD assignments are temporarily suspended. COMPLETED assignments ended normally with matter closure. TERMINATED assignments ended early due to reassignment or other reasons.

products.name: matter_contact
products.description: This association product represents the Role-based assignment between contact and matter. It captures the participation of client contacts in legal matters across multiple functional roles (billing, technical, signatory, decision-maker). Each record links one contact to one matter with attributes that exist only in the context of this relationship, including role on matter, notification preferences, authorization levels, and assignment lifecycle dates.. Existence Justification: In legal practice operations, a single client contact participates in multiple matters simultaneously (e.g., a General Counsel oversees 20+ active matters across different practice areas), and each matter involves multiple client contacts serving different functional roles (billing contact, technical SME, signatory, decision-maker, witness). Law firms actively manage these matter-contact assignments as a distinct operational concept with role-specific attributes, authorization levels, notification preferences, and lifecycle tracking (assignment start/end dates).

products.name: hold_custodian
products.description: This association product represents the assignment of a litigation hold or preservation notice to a specific party who serves as a custodian of potentially relevant ESI (Electronically Stored Information). Each record links one matter_hold to one matter_party (in custodian role) with attributes that track the custodians acknowledgement status, data preservation obligations, collection progress, and compliance with the hold notice. This is a core eDiscovery workflow entity that supports spoliation risk mitigation, proportionality assessment, and regulatory compliance tracking.. Existence Justification: In legal eDiscovery practice, litigation holds are issued to multiple custodians (parties who control potentially relevant ESI), and each custodian may be subject to multiple holds across different matters. Law firms actively manage hold-custodian assignments as distinct operational records, tracking each custodians acknowledgement, data sources, collection status, and compliance obligations. This is not a reference lookup—it is a managed workflow with specialized hold management systems (like Zapproved, Exterro, or Relativity Legal Hold) that track the many-to-many relationship between holds and custodians.

products.name: jurisdiction_practice_coverage

It captures the firm's ability to practice in each jurisdiction-practice area combination, including admission requirements, local counsel needs, and practice restrictions. Each record links one jurisdiction to one practice area with regulatory and operational attributes that exist only in the context of this specific combination.. The firm actively manages this coverage matrix to determine matter acceptance, staffing requirements, and local counsel needs.

products.name: risk_assessment
products.description: This association product represents the Risk Assessment between matter and risk_category. It captures the firm's evaluation of each risk category's applicability and exposure level for each legal matter. Each record links one matter to one risk_category with assessment scores, dates, and review status that exist only in the context of this specific matter-risk combination.. Existence Justification: Legal firms operationally assess each matter against multiple risk categories (cybersecurity, AML, professional indemnity, reputational, data privacy, etc.) as part of their risk management and professional indemnity insurance compliance processes. Each matter-risk combination requires its own assessment with matter-specific inherent and residual risk scores, assessment dates, review cycles, mitigation plans, and risk owners. Risk managers and partners actively create, update, and review these assessments throughout the matter lifecycle.

attributes.description: Date on which this risk category was determined to be applicable to this matter. Marks when the risk was first identified or registered for this matter.

attributes.name: assessed_by
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the risk manager, partner, or committee member who performed or approved the most recent assessment of this matter-risk combination.

attributes.name: assessment_status

products.name: assertion
products.description: This association product represents the assertion of a specific intellectual property asset (patent, trademark, or other IP) within a specific court docket. It captures the operational reality of IP litigation where multiple patents may be asserted in a single case, and a single patent may be asserted across multiple cases. Each record links one docket to one IP asset with attributes that exist only in the context of this specific assertion, including which claims are asserted, invalidity defenses raised, damages theories, and settlement allocations.. Existence Justification: Patent litigation routinely involves multiple patents asserted in a single case (one docket references many IP assets) and individual patents asserted across multiple cases (one IP asset is referenced in many dockets). The business actively manages assertion-specific data including which claims are asserted, invalidity defenses per patent-case pair, damages allocation per patent, and settlement apportionment. This is a core operational relationship in IP litigation practice.

attributes.description: Date when this IP asset was formally asserted in the docket, typically the filing date of the complaint or amended complaint adding this patent to the case.

attributes.name: assertion_status
attributes.description: Current procedural status of this specific patent assertion within the docket. A patent may be withdrawn from a case while other patents remain active, or may be stayed pending IPR while the case proceeds on other patents.

attributes.description: Specification of which claims of the IP asset are asserted in this docket. May reference specific claim numbers (e.g., 'claims 1, 3, 7-12') or indicate all claims. Critical for damages calculation and invalidity analysis.

attributes.description: Damages calculation methodology applied to this specific patent in this case. May include reasonable royalty rate, lost profits allocation, or other theories. Each patent in a multi-patent case may have different damages theories.

attributes.description: Legal theory of infringement for this patent in this case (e.g., direct infringement, induced infringement, contributory infringement). May vary by patent within the same case depending on the accused products and claim scope.

attributes.name: invalidity_defense_raised
attributes.description: Summary of invalidity defenses raised by the defendant specific to this patent in this case. May include anticipation, obviousness, indefiniteness, or other grounds. Varies by patent-case combination.

attributes.description: Portion of settlement amount allocated to this specific patent assertion. Used when a case involving multiple patents settles and the settlement is apportioned across the asserted patents for portfolio valuation and accounting purposes.

products.name: lateral_conflict
products.description: This association product represents the conflict relationship between current firm matters and lateral hire candidate prior matters. It captures the specific conflict analysis performed during lateral attorney screening, documenting which prior matters from the candidate's former firm create conflicts with which current firm matters. Each record links one current matter to one lateral screening with attributes that describe the nature, severity, and mitigation requirements of the specific conflict relationship.. Existence Justification: In legal lateral hire screening, a single lateral candidate may have worked on multiple prior matters at their former firm, each of which may conflict with multiple current firm matters. Conflicts counsel maintain a matter-to-matter conflict matrix where each prior matter is analyzed against each potentially conflicting current matter. The business actively manages this many-to-many relationship, tracking the specific nature of each conflict (adverse party, co-counsel, confidential information overlap), severity level, required mitigation measures, and client consent status for each matter pair.

attributes.description: Unique identifier for this matter-lateral conflict mapping record. Primary key.

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the lateral hire screening record

attributes.name: client_consent_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether informed consent from the client on this current matter is required to proceed with the lateral hire. Required for material conflicts where the client must waive the conflict.

attributes.name: conflict_analysis_date
attributes.description: Date when the conflicts counsel completed the detailed analysis of this specific matter-to-matter conflict relationship. Establishes the timeline of the screening process.

attributes.name: conflict_severity
attributes.description: The severity assessment of this specific matter-to-matter conflict. Disqualifying conflicts prevent hire without client consent. Material conflicts require ethical walls and disclosure. Moderate conflicts require monitoring. Minor conflicts are documented but may not require mitigation. Waivable conflicts can proceed with informed client consent.

attributes.name: disclosure_date
attributes.description: Date when this specific matter conflict was disclosed by the lateral candidate in their screening questionnaire or interview. Establishes the timeline of disclosure for regulatory compliance.

attributes.name: ethical_wall_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether an ethical wall (information barrier) must be established between the lateral hire and this specific current matter. True when the conflict severity and relationship nature require screening the candidate from matter access.

attributes.name: mitigation_notes
attributes.description: Detailed notes on the specific mitigation measures implemented or planned for this matter-lateral conflict pair. Documents ethical wall procedures, client communications, access restrictions, and monitoring requirements.

attributes.name: mitigation_required

attributes.name: prior_matter_role
attributes.description: The role the lateral candidate played on the prior matter at their former firm. Lead attorney and partner roles indicate deeper involvement and higher conflict risk. Support roles may have limited exposure.

attributes.name: relationship_nature
attributes.description: The specific nature of the conflict relationship between the prior matter and current matter. Adverse party indicates the candidate represented a party adverse to a current client. Co-counsel indicates prior joint representation. Same client indicates the candidate represented the same entity. Related party indicates corporate affiliates or related entities. Opposing counsel indicates the candidate was on the opposing side. Confidential info overlap indicates potential access to confidential information relevant to current matter.

attributes.name: substantive_involvement_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the lateral candidate had substantive involvement in the prior matter (vs. administrative or minimal involvement). Substantive involvement increases conflict severity and likelihood of confidential information access.

products.name: matter_control
products.description: This association product represents the implementation and testing of specific risk controls within the context of individual legal matters. It captures the matter-specific application of enterprise risk controls, including control effectiveness ratings, test results, evidence references, and responsible timekeepers for each matter-control pairing. Each record links one matter to one risk control with attributes that exist only in the context of this relationship, enabling matter-level control dashboards and ISO 27001/SRA compliance tracking at the engagement level.. Existence Justification: In legal practice, matters require implementation of multiple risk controls (conflict checks, data protection protocols, billing compliance, privilege management, confidentiality safeguards), and each enterprise risk control is applied across many matters with matter-specific testing, effectiveness ratings, and evidence collection. Law firms actively manage matter-level control dashboards for ISO 27001 certification and SRA compliance reviews, tracking which controls are implemented per engagement, test results, responsible timekeepers, and remediation status. This is an operational many-to-many relationship where the business manages matter-control pairings as distinct compliance records.

attributes.name: extracted_text

attributes.name: file_format

attributes.name: file_hash

attributes.name: file_name

attributes.name: file_size_bytes

attributes.name: is_current_version
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this version is the current authoritative copy of the document. Only one version per document should be marked as current at any time.

attributes.name: language_code
attributes.description: ISO 639-1 two-letter language code of the document content (e.g., 'en', 'fr', 'de'). Detected via Natural Language Processing (NLP) or set manually. Essential for multilingual matter management and translation workflows.

attributes.name: legal_hold_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this version is subject to a legal hold (litigation hold) that suspends normal retention and disposition. Prevents destruction of potentially relevant evidence.
attributes.references: FRCP Rule 37(e), ABA Model Rules of Professional Conduct Rule 3.4

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the last modification to this version's metadata or content. Distinct from created_timestamp; tracks subsequent updates to the version record.

attributes.name: nlp_entities_extracted
attributes.description: JSON or delimited list of named entities extracted from the document via Natural Language Processing (NLP) (e.g., person names, organizations, dates, monetary amounts). Enables advanced search, analytics, and contract intelligence.

attributes.name: ocr_confidence_score
attributes.description: Confidence score (0.00 to 100.00) indicating the OCR engine's certainty in the accuracy of extracted text. Low scores flag documents requiring manual review. Critical for TAR model training quality.

attributes.name: ocr_engine

attributes.name: ocr_processed_flag

attributes.name: page_count

attributes.name: production_date

attributes.name: production_flag

attributes.name: redacted_flag

attributes.name: redaction_reason

attributes.name: retention_category

attributes.name: retention_expiry_date

attributes.name: review_duration_minutes

attributes.name: review_priority

attributes.name: review_start_timestamp

attributes.name: review_status
attributes.description: Current status of the document review assignment in the workflow lifecycle.

attributes.name: review_type

attributes.name: reviewer_comments

attributes.name: modified_timestamp

attributes.name: recipient_names

products.name: esi_custodian
products.description: Identifies individuals or entities whose ESI is subject to legal hold and collection in litigation or investigation matters. Records custodian name, role, organization, data sources held (email systems, file shares, cloud storage, mobile devices), legal hold acknowledgement status, collection status, and interview notes. This is the document-domain view of a person-as-custodian — the authoritative record of their preservation obligations, data map, and collection history. Supports custodian interview workflows and defensible collection planning under FRCP Rule 26, Practice Direction 31B, and GDPR obligations.

products.name: custodian_hold
products.description: This association product represents the assignment of legal hold notices to ESI custodians in litigation and investigation matters. It captures the issuance, acknowledgement, compliance monitoring, and release lifecycle for each custodian-hold pairing. Each record links one custodian to one legal hold with attributes that track the custodians specific preservation obligations, acknowledgement status, interview details, and collection activities under that hold. This is a core eDiscovery workflow entity managed actively throughout the litigation lifecycle.. Existence Justification: In legal eDiscovery practice, legal holds are issued to multiple custodians, and custodians are frequently subject to multiple concurrent legal holds across different matters. Law firms and legal departments actively manage custodian-hold assignments as a distinct workflow: issuing notices, tracking acknowledgements, conducting custodian interviews, monitoring collection progress, and releasing custodians when holds are lifted. This is not a reference relationship—it is an operational business process with its own lifecycle, compliance requirements, and risk management implications governed by FRCP Rule 26 and spoliation case law.

products.name: production_source
products.description: This association product represents the sourcing relationship between eDiscovery production sets and the ESI collections from which they are derived. In eDiscovery workflows, a single production may draw documents from multiple collection events (e.g., combining custodian collections), and a single collection may contribute documents to multiple productions over time (initial production, supplemental production, different matters). Each record captures the subset of documents from a specific collection included in a specific production, along with the Bates numbering applied to that subset and any collection-specific filters or date ranges used during production assembly.. Existence Justification: In eDiscovery operations, production sets routinely draw documents from multiple ESI collection events (e.g., combining collections from different custodians, time periods, or data sources into a single production), and a single collection event commonly contributes documents to multiple productions over the lifecycle of a matter (initial production, supplemental productions, productions for different matters sharing custodians). Legal teams actively manage this many-to-many relationship in platforms like Relativity during production assembly, applying collection-specific Bates ranges, filters, and document counts that exist only in the context of each production-collection pairing.

attributes.description: First Bates number assigned to documents from this collection within this production. Since a production may draw from multiple collections, each collection subset receives its own Bates range within the overall production numbering scheme.

products.name: template_clause_usage
products.description: This association product represents the operational relationship between document templates and clause library entries in the firm's knowledge management system. It captures which clauses are incorporated into which templates, including the clause's position within the template, the specific variant selected, customization notes, and whether the clause is mandatory or optional. Each record represents a deliberate design decision by knowledge management professionals about template composition and is actively managed as templates evolve.. Existence Justification: In legal knowledge management systems, document templates are assembled from multiple reusable clause library entries, and each clause is designed to be reused across multiple templates. Knowledge management teams actively manage these template-clause mappings, making deliberate decisions about which clause variant to use, where to position it, whether it's mandatory, and any template-specific customizations. This is a core operational process in contract automation and template governance.

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to document.legal_document. Business justification: Credit notes reference supporting documents (court orders reducing fees, settlement agreements, billing guideline violations). Required for credit justification, audit trails, and regulatory complianc

attributes.name: practice_area_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to service.practice_area. Business justification: Credit notes impact practice area P&L and require area leader approval. Practice area determines approval authority, revenue adjustment policies, and profitability reporting used in financial manageme

attributes.name: profile_id
attributes.description: Reference to the client entity to whom the credit note is issued. Used for client-level AR reconciliation, realization rate analysis, and financial reporting.
attributes.references: Elite 3E Practice Management and Financial System; American Bar Association (ABA) Model Rules

attributes.name: application_method
attributes.description: Describes how the credit note value was or will be applied. 'applied_to_ar' — offset against an existing outstanding AR balance on the client account; 'cash_refund' — disbursed as a cash payment back to the client; 'held_on_account' — retained as a credit balance for future invoices; 'offset_future_invoice' — earmarked to reduce a specific forthcoming invoice.
attributes.references: Elite 3E Practice Management and Financial System; Aderant Expert Time and Billing; IOLTA Interest on Lawyers Trust Accounts rules

attributes.name: applied_date
attributes.description: The date on which the credit note was applied against an outstanding AR balance or processed as a cash refund. Null if the credit note has not yet been applied (status is 'issued' or 'held'). Used for AR ageing and cash flow reporting.
attributes.references: Elite 3E Practice Management and Financial System; Aderant Expert Time and Billing

attributes.name: approved_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time at which the credit note was formally approved by the authorised approver (approved_by_id). Supports approval workflow audit trails and SOX (Sarbanes-Oxley Act) segregation of duties controls.
attributes.references: Elite 3E Practice Management and Financial System; SOX Section 404; SRA Accounts Rules

attributes.name: billing_guideline_ref
attributes.description: Reference identifier for the client billing guideline or outside counsel guidelines (OCG) provision that triggered or justified this credit note (e.g., a specific guideline clause number). Supports billing guideline compliance tracking and dispute resolution documentation.
attributes.references: Elite 3E Practice Management and Financial System; ABA Model Rules Rule 1.5; SRA Code of Conduct

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time at which the credit note record was first created in the billing system. Serves as the record audit creation timestamp for data lineage, audit trail, and GDPR (General Data Protection Regulation) data processing records.
attributes.references: Elite 3E Practice Management and Financial System; GDPR Article 5; SOX Section 404

attributes.name: credit_note_number
attributes.description: Externally visible, human-readable unique identifier for the credit note as printed on the document issued to the client. Follows the firm's sequential numbering convention (e.g., CN-2024-000123). Used in client correspondence, remittance matching, and LEDES electronic billing submissions.
attributes.references: Elite 3E Practice Management and Financial System; LEDES 1998B Standard; Aderant Expert Time and Billing

attributes.name: credit_note_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the credit note. 'draft' — prepared but not yet issued; 'issued' — sent to client; 'applied' — offset against an outstanding AR balance; 'refunded' — cash refund disbursed to client; 'held' — held on account for future application; 'voided' — cancelled and reversed.
attributes.references: Elite 3E Practice Management and Financial System; Aderant Expert Time and Billing

attributes.name: credit_reason_code
attributes.description: Standardised classification of the business reason for issuing the credit note. 'overbilling' — fees or disbursements billed in excess of agreed rates; 'dispute_resolution' — credit issued as part of a formal billing dispute settlement; 'goodwill_adjustment' — discretionary reduction to maintain client relationship; 'fee_cap_correction' — invoice exceeded an agreed AFA (Alternative Fee Arrangement) or matter budget cap; 'billing_error' — administrative or data entry error on the original invoice; 'write_off' — uncollectable amount formally written off. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: overbilling|dispute_resolution|goodwill_adjustment|fee_cap_correction|billing_error|write_off — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Elite 3E Practice Management and Financial System; ABA Model Rules of Professional Conduct Rule 1.5 (Fees); Solicitors Regulation Authority (SRA) Code of Conduct

attributes.name: credit_reason_narrative
attributes.description: Free-text description providing the detailed business justification for the credit note, supplementing the structured credit_reason_code. May reference specific time entries, disbursements, or billing guideline violations. Classified confidential as it may contain commercially sensitive negotiation details or LPP (Legal Professional Privilege) adjacent information.
attributes.references: ABA Model Rules of Professional Conduct Rule 1.5; SRA Code of Conduct; GDPR Article 5 (data minimisation)

attributes.name: credit_type
attributes.description: Categorises the nature of the credit note by the component of the original invoice being reversed. 'fee_credit' — applies only to professional fees; 'disbursement_credit' — applies only to disbursements and expenses; 'tax_credit' — applies only to the tax component; 'combined' — spans multiple invoice components.
attributes.references: Elite 3E Practice Management and Financial System; LEDES 1998B Standard; UTBMS Uniform Task-Based Management System

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code in which the credit note amounts are denominated (e.g., USD, GBP, EUR). Required for multi-currency billing environments and foreign exchange (FX) reporting.
attributes.references: ISO 4217 Currency Codes; Elite 3E Practice Management and Financial System

attributes.name: disbursement_credit_amount
attributes.description: The amount of disbursements and client-chargeable expenses being credited on this credit note. Includes hard costs (court filing fees, expert witness fees) and soft costs (photocopying, courier). Expressed in the billing currency.
attributes.references: Elite 3E Practice Management and Financial System; Aderant Expert Time and Billing

attributes.name: dispute_reference
attributes.description: Reference number or identifier for the formal billing dispute, client complaint, or ADR (Alternative Dispute Resolution) proceeding that gave rise to this credit note. Populated when credit_reason_code is 'dispute_resolution'. Classified confidential due to commercially sensitive negotiation context.
attributes.references: Elite 3E Practice Management and Financial System; ABA Model Rules Rule 1.5; SRA Code of Conduct; ADR Alternative Dispute Resolution frameworks

attributes.name: exchange_rate
attributes.description: The foreign exchange rate applied to convert the credit note amounts from the billing currency to the firm's functional (home) currency at the time of issuance. Required for multi-currency consolidation and financial reporting under IFRS/US GAAP.
attributes.references: Elite 3E Practice Management and Financial System; IFRS 21 Effects of Changes in Foreign Exchange Rates; US GAAP ASC 830

attributes.name: fee_arrangement_type
attributes.description: The type of fee arrangement (AFA — Alternative Fee Arrangement) under which the original invoice was billed and against which this credit note is issued. Determines the financial impact on realization rate calculations and AFA performance tracking.
attributes.references: Elite 3E Practice Management and Financial System; ABA Model Rules Rule 1.5; UTBMS Uniform Task-Based Management System

attributes.name: fee_credit_amount
attributes.description: The gross amount of professional fees being credited or reversed on this credit note, expressed in the billing currency. Represents the pre-tax fee reduction. Used in realization rate analysis and WIP (Work in Progress) reconciliation.
attributes.references: Elite 3E Practice Management and Financial System; Aderant Expert Time and Billing; ABA Model Rules Rule 1.5

attributes.name: functional_currency_amount
attributes.description: The total credit note amount converted to the firm's functional (home) currency using the exchange_rate at issuance date. Used for consolidated financial reporting, GL (General Ledger) posting, and partner profit calculations (PPP/PEP).
attributes.references: Elite 3E Practice Management and Financial System; IFRS 21; US GAAP ASC 830; SOX Section 404

attributes.name: gl_account_code
attributes.description: The GL (General Ledger) account code to which the credit note is posted in the firm's accounting system. Required for financial close, trial balance reconciliation, and SOX (Sarbanes-Oxley Act) internal controls compliance.
attributes.references: Elite 3E Practice Management and Financial System; SOX Section 404; US GAAP; IFRS 15 Revenue from Contracts with Customers

attributes.name: issued_date
attributes.description: The calendar date on which the credit note was formally issued and transmitted to the client. This is the principal business event date for the credit note lifecycle, used for AR ageing, period-end close, and tax reporting.
attributes.references: Elite 3E Practice Management and Financial System; ABA Model Rules; HMRC VAT Notice 700

attributes.name: originating_invoice_date
attributes.description: The issuance date of the original invoice being credited. Used to calculate the elapsed time between invoice issuance and credit note issuance for billing dispute analytics and SLA (Service Level Agreement) compliance reporting.
attributes.references: Elite 3E Practice Management and Financial System; LEDES 1998B Standard

attributes.name: originating_invoice_number
attributes.description: The human-readable invoice number of the original invoice being reversed or reduced by this credit note. Stored as a denormalised reference to support client-facing documents and LEDES electronic billing submissions without requiring a join.
attributes.references: Elite 3E Practice Management and Financial System; LEDES 1998B Standard

attributes.name: pro_bono_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the credit note relates to a pro bono matter (True) or a standard commercial matter (False). Required for pro bono reporting to the ABA (American Bar Association) and Law Society, and for exclusion from commercial realization rate calculations.
attributes.references: ABA Model Rules Rule 6.1 (Voluntary Pro Bono Publico Service); Law Society of England and Wales Pro Bono Protocol

attributes.name: source_system_code
attributes.description: Identifies the operational system of record from which this credit note record originated. 'elite_3e' — Elite 3E Practice Management and Financial System; 'aderant_expert' — Aderant Expert Time and Billing; 'manual' — manually entered outside a primary system. Required for data lineage and reconciliation in the Databricks Silver Layer.
attributes.references: Elite 3E Practice Management and Financial System; Aderant Expert Time and Billing; Databricks Lakehouse Silver Layer data lineage standards

attributes.name: tax_credit_amount
attributes.description: The tax component (e.g., VAT, GST, sales tax) being reversed or adjusted on this credit note. Must be reported separately for tax authority compliance and VAT/GST return reconciliation.
attributes.references: Elite 3E Practice Management and Financial System; HMRC VAT Notice 700; IRS Publication 15; GDPR Article 5

attributes.name: tax_jurisdiction_code
attributes.description: ISO country or sub-national jurisdiction code identifying the tax authority under which the VAT, GST, or sales tax credit is calculated and reported. Required for multi-jurisdictional tax compliance and VAT/GST return reconciliation.
attributes.references: Elite 3E Practice Management and Financial System; HMRC VAT Notice 700; EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC; IRS Publication 15; GDPR Article 5

attributes.name: tax_rate_pct
attributes.description: The applicable tax rate (as a percentage) used to calculate the tax_credit_amount on this credit note. Stored for audit trail purposes as tax rates may change over time.
attributes.references: Elite 3E Practice Management and Financial System; HMRC VAT Notice 700; EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC; IRS Publication 15

attributes.name: total_credit_amount
attributes.description: The total gross value of the credit note inclusive of fees, disbursements, and tax adjustments (fee_credit_amount + disbursement_credit_amount + tax_credit_amount). This is the net amount by which the client's AR balance is reduced or refunded. Core field for AR reconciliation and financial reporting.
attributes.references: Elite 3E Practice Management and Financial System; Aderant Expert Time and Billing; SOX Section 404

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time at which the credit note record was last modified in the billing system. Used for incremental data pipeline processing, change data capture (CDC), and audit trail maintenance.
attributes.references: Elite 3E Practice Management and Financial System; GDPR Article 5; SOX Section 404

attributes.name: utbms_task_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: Uniform Task-Based Management System (UTBMS) Task Code
attributes.description: The UTBMS (Uniform Task-Based Management System) task code associated with the primary fee component being credited. Used in task-based billing analysis and client billing guideline compliance reporting.
attributes.references: UTBMS Uniform Task-Based Management System; LEDES 1998B Standard; ABA Model Rules

attributes.name: voided_date
attributes.description: The date on which the credit note was voided or cancelled. Populated only when credit_note_status is 'voided'. Required for audit trail and period-end reversal processing.
attributes.references: Elite 3E Practice Management and Financial System; SOX Section 404

attributes.name: write_off_approved_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the credit note has been formally approved as a write-off (True) by the authorised partner or finance committee. Relevant when credit_reason_code is 'write_off'. Required for bad debt provisioning, GL (General Ledger) write-off posting, and SOX (Sarbanes-Oxley Act) internal controls.
attributes.references: Elite 3E Practice Management and Financial System; SOX Section 404; US GAAP ASC 310; IFRS 9 Financial Instruments

attributes.name: primary_credit_invoice_id
attributes.description: Reference to the originating invoice against which this credit note is issued. Establishes the parent-child relationship between the credit note and the billed invoice for accounts receivable (AR) reconciliation.
attributes.references: Elite 3E Practice Management and Financial System; LEDES 1998B Standard

attributes.name: primary_credit_matter_id
attributes.description: Reference to the legal matter or case associated with the credit note. Enables matter-level profitability analysis and WIP (Work in Progress) reconciliation.
attributes.references: Elite 3E Practice Management and Financial System; UTBMS Uniform Task-Based Management System

attributes.name: primary_credit_timekeeper_id
attributes.description: Reference to the responsible billing attorney (timekeeper) accountable for the matter on which the credit note is issued. Used for partner-level financial performance reporting including PPP (Profit Per Partner) and RPE (Revenue Per Equity Partner).
attributes.references: Elite 3E Practice Management and Financial System; Aderant Expert Time and Billing

attributes.name: billing_period_end_date
attributes.description: The end date of the billing period covered by the original invoice being credited. Together with billing_period_start_date, defines the revenue recognition period affected by this credit note.
attributes.references: Elite 3E Practice Management and Financial System; IFRS 15; US GAAP ASC 606

attributes.name: billing_period_start_date
attributes.description: The start date of the billing period covered by the original invoice being credited. Used to attribute the credit note to the correct accounting period for revenue recognition and WIP (Work in Progress) reversal.
attributes.references: Elite 3E Practice Management and Financial System; IFRS 15 Revenue from Contracts with Customers; US GAAP ASC 606

attributes.name: office_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the firm office or branch responsible for the matter associated with this credit note. Used for office-level financial reporting, GL (General Ledger) cost centre allocation, and geographic revenue analysis.
attributes.references: Elite 3E Practice Management and Financial System; Aderant Expert Time and Billing
