products.name: rating_scale
products.description: Master reference table for rating_scale. Referenced by rating_scale_id.

attributes.name: rating_scale_id
attributes.description: Primary key for rating_scale

attributes.name: allows_decimal_precision
attributes.description: Indicates whether the rating scale permits decimal precision beyond half-points (e.g., 3.75, 4.25). True if decimal precision is allowed, False otherwise.

attributes.name: allows_half_points
attributes.description: Indicates whether the rating scale permits half-point increments (e.g., 3.5 on a 1-5 scale). True if half-points are allowed, False if only whole numbers are permitted.

attributes.name: applicable_to_attorneys
attributes.description: Indicates whether this rating scale is used for attorney performance evaluations, competency assessments, or partner reviews. True if applicable to attorneys, False otherwise.

attributes.name: applicable_to_partners
attributes.description: Indicates whether this rating scale is used for equity partner, non-equity partner, or senior partner evaluations. True if applicable to partners, False otherwise.

attributes.name: applicable_to_staff
attributes.description: Indicates whether this rating scale is used for non-attorney staff evaluations (paralegals, legal assistants, administrative staff). True if applicable to staff, False otherwise.

attributes.name: approval_level
attributes.description: The organizational level required to approve ratings using this scale: none (no approval needed), manager (direct supervisor), practice_leader (practice group head), compensation_committee (firm compensation committee), managing_partner (firm managing partner).

attributes.name: approval_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether ratings using this scale require formal approval by a manager, practice group leader, or compensation committee before being finalized. True if approval is required, False otherwise.

attributes.name: comments_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether evaluators must provide written comments or justification when assigning ratings using this scale. True if comments are mandatory, False otherwise.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this rating scale record was first created in the system. Audit field for data lineage and compliance.

attributes.name: display_order
attributes.description: Numeric value controlling the display order of this rating scale in user interfaces and selection lists. Lower numbers appear first.

attributes.name: distribution_curve_type
attributes.description: The type of distribution curve applied when forced distribution is required: none (no forced distribution), bell_curve (normal distribution), top_grading (A/B/C player model), rank_and_yank (bottom percentage must be rated low).

attributes.name: effective_end_date
attributes.description: The date on which this rating scale is retired or replaced. Null if the scale is currently active with no planned end date.

attributes.name: effective_start_date
attributes.description: The date from which this rating scale becomes active and available for use in performance evaluations and assessments.

attributes.name: excellence_threshold
attributes.description: The rating value at or above which performance is considered excellent or exceeds expectations. Used for identifying high performers and bonus eligibility.

attributes.name: forced_distribution_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether this rating scale requires forced distribution (e.g., only 20% can receive the highest rating, 10% must be in the lowest tier). True if forced distribution applies, False otherwise.

attributes.name: increment_step
attributes.description: The numeric increment between valid rating values (e.g., 1.0 for integer scales, 0.5 for half-point scales, 0.1 for decimal scales).

attributes.name: is_default_scale
attributes.description: Indicates whether this is the default rating scale used when no specific scale is designated for a performance review or assessment. True if this is the default scale, False otherwise.

attributes.name: linked_to_compensation
attributes.description: Indicates whether ratings on this scale directly influence compensation decisions such as bonuses, salary increases, or profit-sharing distributions. True if linked to compensation, False otherwise.

attributes.name: linked_to_promotion
attributes.description: Indicates whether ratings on this scale are a factor in promotion decisions (e.g., associate to senior associate, counsel to partner). True if linked to promotion, False otherwise.

attributes.name: maximum_value
attributes.description: The highest numeric value on the rating scale (e.g., 5 for a 1-5 scale, 100 for a 0-100 scale).

attributes.name: midpoint_value
attributes.description: The midpoint or neutral value on the rating scale, often representing meets expectations or satisfactory performance.

attributes.name: minimum_value
attributes.description: The lowest numeric value on the rating scale (e.g., 1 for a 1-5 scale, 0 for a 0-100 scale).

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this rating scale record was last updated. Audit field for change tracking and data governance.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Additional notes, guidance, or instructions for evaluators using this rating scale. May include examples of behaviors or performance indicators for each rating level.

attributes.name: passing_threshold
attributes.description: The minimum rating value required to be considered passing or acceptable performance. Used in competency assessments and mandatory training evaluations.

attributes.name: peer_review_allowed
attributes.description: Indicates whether this rating scale can be used for peer-to-peer evaluations (e.g., associate reviewing another associate, partner reviewing another partner). True if peer review is allowed, False otherwise.

attributes.name: requires_calibration
attributes.description: Indicates whether ratings using this scale must go through a calibration process with peer review or management committee to ensure consistency across evaluators. True if calibration is required, False otherwise.

attributes.name: scale_code
attributes.description: Short alphanumeric code uniquely identifying the rating scale for system integration and reporting (e.g., PERF-5PT, COMP-10PT, PARTNER-EVAL).

attributes.name: scale_description
attributes.description: Detailed business description of the rating scale, its purpose, and usage context within performance management, talent development, or compensation processes.

attributes.name: scale_direction
attributes.description: Indicates whether higher values represent better performance (ascending) or lower values represent better performance (descending). Most legal industry scales are ascending.

attributes.name: scale_name
attributes.description: The business name of the rating scale (e.g., Annual Performance Review Scale, Partner Evaluation Scale, Associate Competency Scale).

attributes.name: scale_type
attributes.description: Categorical classification of the rating scale purpose: performance (annual reviews), competency (skill assessments), potential (succession planning), behavior (conduct evaluations), skill (technical proficiency), client_feedback (client satisfaction).

attributes.name: self_assessment_allowed
attributes.description: Indicates whether timekeepers can use this rating scale to perform self-assessments as part of the performance review process. True if self-assessment is allowed, False otherwise.

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: The system of record where this rating scale is defined and maintained (e.g., SAP SuccessFactors, Workday HCM, custom HRIS).

attributes.name: usage_context
attributes.description: The primary business context in which this rating scale is applied: annual_review (year-end performance), mid_year_review (interim check-in), probation_review (new hire evaluation), promotion_review (advancement consideration), compensation_review (bonus and salary decisions), succession_planning (leadership pipeline assessment).

attributes.name: version_number
attributes.description: Version identifier for the rating scale to track changes over time (e.g., v1.0, v2.1, 2024.1). Used when scales are updated or refined.

attributes.name: external_system_id
attributes.description: The unique identifier for this rating scale in the source system (e.g., SAP SuccessFactors rating scale ID). Used for system integration and data reconciliation.

attributes.name: status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the rating scale: active (in use), inactive (temporarily suspended), draft (under development), retired (no longer used), under_review (being evaluated for changes).

attributes.name: superseded_rating_scale_id
attributes.description: Self-referencing FK on rating_scale (superseded_rating_scale_id)

domains.name: service
domains.description: Catalog of legal service offerings such as M&A advisory, litigation, IP counsel, regulatory compliance counseling, employment law, and advisory packages. Manages service definitions, practice area taxonomy, pricing models, SLA terms, and service-to-matter mappings enabling business development and RFP responses.
domains.references: ABA Model Rules; Microsoft Dynamics 365 CRM

products.name: practice_area
products.description: Master taxonomy of legal practice areas and sub-specializations offered by the firm (e.g., M&A, Litigation, IP, Employment Law, Regulatory Compliance, Real Estate). Supports hierarchical parent-child classification enabling roll-up reporting. Each practice area carries a unique code, description, active/inactive status, and regulatory body alignment. Used to categorize matters, timekeepers, service offerings, and rate cards across all firm systems.

attributes.name: practice_area_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the practice area. Primary key for the practice area master taxonomy.

attributes.name: category_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to risk.risk_category. Business justification: Practice areas map to inherent risk categories (litigation = PI exposure, regulatory = compliance risk, corporate = conflict risk). Insurance allocation, conflict screening protocols, and risk managem

attributes.name: parent_practice_area_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent practice area in the hierarchical taxonomy, enabling roll-up reporting from sub-specializations to broader practice groups. Null for top-level practice areas.

attributes.name: average_matter_value
attributes.description: Historical average total billed value for matters in this practice area, used for pipeline valuation, revenue forecasting, and business development targeting. Expressed in firm base currency.

attributes.name: billable_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether time and disbursements in this practice area are typically billable to clients. False for internal practice areas such as professional development, pro bono coordination, or firm administration.

attributes.name: classification_type
attributes.description: High-level classification of the practice area by the nature of legal work performed. Transactional covers M&A (Mergers and Acquisitions), corporate deals; Advisory covers counseling and opinions; Litigation covers dispute resolution; Regulatory covers compliance and government relations; Hybrid covers mixed-mode practices; Specialized covers niche areas like IP (Intellectual Property) prosecution.
attributes.references: American Bar Association (ABA) Practice Area Taxonomy

attributes.name: cpd_requirement_hours
attributes.description: Annual CPD (Continuing Professional Development) or CLE (Continuing Legal Education) hours required for timekeepers practicing in this area, as mandated by the governing regulatory body. Used for compliance tracking and training program planning.
attributes.references: American Bar Association (ABA) Model Rule for Continuing Legal Education, Solicitors Regulation Authority (SRA) CPD Requirements

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this practice area record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: default_billing_arrangement
attributes.description: The most common fee arrangement type for matters in this practice area. Hourly for traditional time-based billing; Fixed Fee for scoped project work; Contingency for plaintiff litigation; AFA (Alternative Fee Arrangement) for value-based or risk-sharing models; Retainer for ongoing advisory; Capped Fee for budget-certainty arrangements; Blended Rate for team-based pricing; Success Fee for outcome-based compensation. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: hourly|fixed_fee|contingency|afa|retainer|capped_fee|blended_rate|success_fee — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: LEDES (Legal Electronic Data Exchange Standard) Billing Guidelines, American Bar Association (ABA) Model Rules 1.5

attributes.name: effective_from_date
attributes.description: Date from which this practice area definition became effective and available for matter classification and timekeeper assignment. Used for historical reporting and taxonomy versioning.

attributes.name: effective_to_date
attributes.description: Date on which this practice area definition ceased to be effective. Null for currently active practice areas. Used for historical reporting and taxonomy evolution tracking.

attributes.name: external_reference_code
attributes.description: External or client-facing practice area code used in RFP (Request for Proposal) responses, pitch materials, or industry benchmarking surveys. May differ from internal code for marketing or competitive positioning reasons.

attributes.name: hierarchy_level
attributes.description: Numeric depth of this practice area in the hierarchical taxonomy. Level 1 represents top-level practice groups, Level 2 represents major practice areas, Level 3+ represents sub-specializations. Enables hierarchical roll-up queries and reporting.

attributes.name: hierarchy_path
attributes.description: Materialized path representing the full lineage from root to this practice area, typically formatted as slash-separated IDs or codes (e.g., /CORP/MA/CROSSBORDER). Optimizes hierarchical queries and enables efficient ancestor/descendant lookups.

attributes.name: insurance_coverage_requirement
attributes.description: Specific professional indemnity or malpractice insurance coverage requirements for this practice area, including minimum coverage amounts and specialized endorsements. Critical for high-risk areas like securities litigation, M&A (Mergers and Acquisitions), or medical malpractice defense.
attributes.references: American Bar Association (ABA) Model Rule 1.4, Solicitors Regulation Authority (SRA) Indemnity Insurance Rules

attributes.name: jurisdiction_scope
attributes.description: Geographic or legal jurisdiction scope for this practice area. May be a single jurisdiction (e.g., New York, England and Wales), multi-jurisdictional (e.g., US Federal, EU), or global. Critical for conflict checking, regulatory compliance, and timekeeper licensing requirements.

attributes.name: knowledge_management_category
attributes.description: Classification used by the firms knowledge management system to organize precedents, practice notes, standard documents, and checklists for this practice area. Maps to DMS (Document Management System) taxonomy and knowledge repository structure.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this practice area record was last updated. Used for change tracking, audit trail, and data synchronization across systems.

attributes.name: practice_area_code
attributes.description: Short alphanumeric code uniquely identifying the practice area across all firm systems. Used in matter coding, timekeeper assignments, and rate card structures.

attributes.name: practice_area_description
attributes.description: Detailed narrative describing the scope, services, and typical matters handled within this practice area. Used for RFP (Request for Proposal) responses, business development materials, and knowledge management.

attributes.name: practice_area_name
attributes.description: Full business name of the practice area as recognized by clients and used in marketing materials, engagement letters, and matter classifications.
attributes.references: American Bar Association (ABA) Practice Area Taxonomy

attributes.name: practice_area_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the practice area. Active areas are available for new matter intake and timekeeper assignment. Inactive areas are no longer offered but may have legacy matters. Suspended areas are temporarily unavailable. Archived areas are historical records only.

attributes.name: practice_group
attributes.description: Broader practice group or department to which this practice area belongs, enabling organizational roll-up and resource allocation reporting.

attributes.name: primary_service_line
attributes.description: The primary revenue-generating service line or business unit to which this practice area contributes. Used for P&L (Profit and Loss) allocation, partner compensation, and strategic planning.

attributes.name: pro_bono_eligible
attributes.description: Indicates whether this practice area is commonly used for pro bono matters. True for areas like immigration, civil rights, family law; False for highly specialized commercial areas. Used for pro bono reporting and CLE (Continuing Legal Education) credit tracking.
attributes.references: American Bar Association (ABA) Model Rule 6.1 Pro Bono Publico Service

attributes.name: regulatory_body_alignment
attributes.description: Primary regulatory or professional body whose standards, ethics rules, and CPD (Continuing Professional Development) requirements govern this practice area. Examples include ABA (American Bar Association), SRA (Solicitors Regulation Authority), IBA (International Bar Association), state bar associations, or specialized bodies like USPTO for IP (Intellectual Property) practice.
attributes.references: American Bar Association (ABA), Solicitors Regulation Authority (SRA), International Bar Association (IBA)

attributes.name: requires_security_clearance
attributes.description: Indicates whether timekeepers working in this practice area typically require government or client security clearance due to the nature of matters (e.g., defense contracting, national security, classified government work).

attributes.name: requires_specialization
attributes.description: Indicates whether this practice area requires specialized certification, licensing, or accreditation beyond general legal practice admission. True for areas like patent prosecution (USPTO registration), tax law (CPA or LLM), or admiralty law (specialized bar admission).
attributes.references: American Bar Association (ABA) Model Rules of Professional Conduct

attributes.name: short_name
attributes.description: Abbreviated name or acronym for the practice area used in internal reporting, dashboards, and space-constrained displays.

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Name of the operational system of record from which this practice area definition originated. Typically Elite 3E practice area master, but may include legacy systems or manual taxonomy management tools.

attributes.name: technology_platform_requirement
attributes.description: Specialized technology platforms or tools typically required for matters in this practice area. Examples: Relativity for eDiscovery (Electronic Discovery) in litigation; LexisNexis for legal research; CLM (Contract Lifecycle Management) systems for transactional work; IP (Intellectual Property) docketing systems for patent prosecution.

attributes.name: typical_matter_duration_days
attributes.description: Average or median duration in days for matters in this practice area, from matter opening to closure. Used for resource planning, pipeline forecasting, and WIP (Work in Progress) aging analysis. Null for ongoing advisory relationships without defined end dates.

attributes.name: utbms_activity_code_prefix
attributes.business_glossary_term: Uniform Task-Based Management System (UTBMS) Activity Code Prefix
attributes.description: Standard UTBMS (Uniform Task-Based Management System) activity code prefix applicable to this practice area, providing granular activity-level coding for time entries and expense tracking in client billing.
attributes.references: UTBMS (Uniform Task-Based Management System) Code Set, LEDES (Legal Electronic Data Exchange Standard)

attributes.name: utbms_task_code_prefix
attributes.business_glossary_term: Uniform Task-Based Management System (UTBMS) Task Code Prefix
attributes.description: Standard UTBMS (Uniform Task-Based Management System) task code prefix applicable to this practice area, enabling standardized time entry coding and client billing compliance. Examples: L for Litigation, C for Case Management, A for ADR (Alternative Dispute Resolution), T for Transactional.
attributes.references: UTBMS (Uniform Task-Based Management System) Code Set, LEDES (Legal Electronic Data Exchange Standard)

products.name: legal_service

This is the SSOT for what the firm offers commercially and operationally, used in RFP responses, engagement letters (LOE), and business development pipelines in Microsoft Dynamics 365.

attributes.name: legal_service_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the legal service offering. Primary key for the legal service catalog.

attributes.name: attorney_profile_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the partner responsible for this service offering's definition, quality, pricing, and strategic positioning. Links to the workforce or partner master data.

attributes.name: category_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to risk.risk_category. Business justification: Legal services are classified by inherent risk category (M&A = conflict risk, IP = PI exposure). Risk-based pricing, insurance requirements, and partner approval thresholds depend on this classificati

attributes.name: line_id

attributes.name: approval_required

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this service offering record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage.

attributes.name: cross_sell_services
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of related service codes that are commonly cross-sold or bundled with this offering. Used in business development, client relationship management, and revenue optimization.

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the standard rate. Supports multi-currency pricing for international service offerings.

attributes.name: deliverable_types
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of typical deliverable types produced by this service. Examples include legal opinions, contracts, court filings, compliance reports, due diligence memoranda, or advisory presentations.

attributes.name: effective_date

attributes.name: eligible_client_segments
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of client segments or types eligible for this service offering. attributes.name: estimated_duration_hours

attributes.name: expiration_date

attributes.name: jurisdiction_coverage

attributes.name: knowledge_assets

attributes.name: matter_type_mapping

attributes.name: modified_by_user
attributes.description: Username or identifier of the user who last modified this service offering record. Supports audit trail and accountability.

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this service offering record was last modified. Used for audit trail, change tracking, and data synchronization.

attributes.name: next_review_date

attributes.name: practice_area

attributes.name: regulatory_framework

attributes.name: required_expertise_level

attributes.name: service_category

attributes.name: service_code

attributes.name: service_description

attributes.name: service_name

attributes.name: service_status

attributes.name: service_type

attributes.name: sla_delivery_time_days

attributes.description: Committed delivery timeframe in business days from engagement to completion, as defined in Service Level Agreement (SLA) terms. Used in client commitments and matter planning.

attributes.name: sla_response_time_hours
attributes.business_glossary_term: Service Level Agreement (SLA) Response Time Hours
attributes.description: Committed response time in hours from service request to initial engagement or acknowledgment, as defined in Service Level Agreement (SLA) terms for this offering.

attributes.name: standard_rate
attributes.description: Standard billing rate or base fee for this service offering in the firm's primary operating currency. For hourly services, represents the blended or standard hourly rate. For fixed-fee services, represents the base package price.

attributes.name: technology_requirements
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of specialized technology platforms or tools required to deliver this service. Examples include eDiscovery platforms, contract lifecycle management systems, legal research databases, or document automation tools.

attributes.name: utbms_task_codes
attributes.business_glossary_term: Uniform Task-Based Management System (UTBMS) Task Codes
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of Uniform Task-Based Management System (UTBMS) task codes associated with this service offering. Used for time entry classification, billing, and client reporting in LEDES format.
attributes.references: UTBMS (Uniform Task-Based Management System) Code Set

attributes.name: legal_practice_area_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to service.practice_area. Business justification: Each legal service belongs to a practice area. Normalize by linking to practice_area master taxonomy. The practice_area STRING column is a code/name reference.

products.name: tier
products.description: Defines the tiered packaging levels for legal services (e.g., Standard, Premium, Enterprise, Bespoke). Each tier specifies the scope of coverage, included deliverables, response commitments, and eligibility for alternative fee arrangements (AFA). Used to structure RFP responses and engagement letter (LOE) terms. Enables differentiated pricing and SLA assignment across client segments.

attributes.name: tier_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the service tier. Primary key.

attributes.name: appetite_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to risk.risk_appetite. Business justification: Service tiers define firm risk appetite boundaries (premium tier = higher complexity tolerance, standard tier = conservative limits). Engagement acceptance workflows verify matter risk profile against

attributes.name: practice_area_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to service.practice_area. Business justification: Service tiers are defined per practice area. Normalize by linking to practice_area master. The practice_area STRING column is just a code/name reference.

attributes.name: segment_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to client.client_segment. Business justification: Service tiers explicitly target client segments (premium tier for top-tier clients, standard for mid-market). Tier eligibility, SLA commitments, and pricing are segment-driven. Removes denormalized cl

attributes.name: afa_eligible_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this tier is eligible for Alternative Fee Arrangements (AFA) such as fixed fees, capped fees, or success-based pricing. True if AFA options are available; False if only hourly billing applies.
attributes.references: American Bar Association (ABA) Model Rules of Professional Conduct

attributes.name: afa_models_supported
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of AFA models supported for this tier (e.g., Fixed Fee, Capped Fee, Blended Rate, Success Fee, Retainer). Used in pricing discussions and engagement structuring.
attributes.references: American Bar Association (ABA) Model Rules of Professional Conduct

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: Date on which this service tier configuration was approved. Used for governance and audit trail.

attributes.name: approval_status
attributes.description: Current approval status of this service tier configuration. Only approved tiers are available for engagement assignment. Used in governance workflow.

attributes.name: approved_by_partner
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the partner who approved this service tier configuration. Used for governance and accountability.

attributes.name: base_hourly_rate
attributes.description: Standard hourly billing rate for this tier in the firm's base currency. Used as the starting point for rate negotiations and engagement pricing. May vary by timekeeper seniority within the tier.

attributes.name: conflict_check_level
attributes.description: Level of conflict checking required for engagements under this tier (standard, enhanced, comprehensive). Higher tiers may require more rigorous conflict analysis and ethical wall procedures.
attributes.references: American Bar Association (ABA) Model Rules of Professional Conduct Rule 1.7

attributes.name: created_by_user
attributes.description: Username or identifier of the user who created this service tier record. Used for audit trail and accountability.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this service tier record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage.

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the base hourly rate and pricing (e.g., USD, GBP, EUR). Used in multi-currency billing and financial reporting.

attributes.name: data_protection_classification
attributes.description: Data protection and confidentiality classification level for matters under this tier (standard, confidential, highly_confidential). Determines document handling, access controls, and encryption requirements.

attributes.name: document_retention_years
attributes.description: Minimum document retention period in years for matters under this tier, as required by regulatory obligations and professional standards. Used in records management and DMS configuration.
attributes.references: American Bar Association (ABA) Model Rules of Professional Conduct Rule 1.15, Jurisdiction-Specific Bar Rules

attributes.name: effective_end_date
attributes.description: Date on which this service tier is no longer available for new engagements. Null for currently active tiers. Used in service catalog versioning and deprecation management.

attributes.name: effective_start_date
attributes.description: Date from which this service tier becomes available for new engagements. Used in service catalog versioning and pricing transitions.

attributes.name: included_deliverables
attributes.description: Comma-separated or structured list of standard deliverables included in the tier (e.g., legal opinions, memoranda, contract drafts, compliance checklists). Used in RFP responses and engagement scoping.

attributes.name: insurance_coverage_required_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Professional Indemnity Insurance Coverage Required Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether specific professional indemnity insurance coverage or coverage limits are required for engagements under this tier. True if additional coverage is mandatory; False otherwise.
attributes.references: Solicitors Regulation Authority (SRA) Indemnity Insurance Rules

attributes.name: kyc_aml_level
attributes.business_glossary_term: Know Your Client (KYC) and Anti-Money Laundering (AML) Level
attributes.description: Level of KYC and AML due diligence required for clients engaging under this tier (basic, standard, enhanced, high_risk). Higher tiers or higher-risk practice areas may require enhanced due diligence.

attributes.name: last_modified_by_user
attributes.description: Username or identifier of the user who last modified this service tier record. Used for audit trail and accountability.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this service tier record was last modified. Used for audit trail and change tracking.

attributes.name: matter_type_applicability
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of matter types or case categories to which this tier applies (e.g., Transactional, Litigation, Advisory, Compliance). Used in matter intake and service assignment.
attributes.references: Uniform Task-Based Management System (UTBMS) Matter Type Codes

attributes.name: maximum_engagement_value
attributes.description: Maximum total engagement value or cap applicable to this tier (if any). Null for uncapped tiers. Used in pricing and risk management.

attributes.name: minimum_engagement_value
attributes.description: Minimum total engagement value or retainer amount required to qualify for this tier. Used in client segmentation and engagement acceptance decisions.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes or comments regarding this service tier, including special terms, exceptions, or usage guidance. Used by practice managers and business development teams.

attributes.name: partner_approval_required_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether partner-level approval is required to assign a matter to this tier. True if approval is mandatory; False if associates or practice managers can assign. Used in engagement workflow and governance.

attributes.name: practice_area
attributes.description: Primary practice area or legal service line to which this tier applies (e.g., M&A, Litigation, IP Counsel, Regulatory Compliance, Employment Law). Aligns with firm practice area taxonomy. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: M&A|Litigation|IP Counsel|Regulatory Compliance|Employment Law|Corporate Transactions|Dispute Resolution|Real Estate|Tax|Labor & Employment — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: American Bar Association (ABA) Practice Area Taxonomy

attributes.name: response_time_commitment_hours
attributes.description: Maximum response time commitment in hours for initial client inquiries or urgent requests under this tier. Forms part of the Service Level Agreement (SLA) terms.

attributes.name: scope_of_coverage
attributes.description: Detailed definition of the legal services and deliverables included in this tier (e.g., advisory opinions, document review, representation in proceedings, regulatory filings). Used to set client expectations and scope engagement letters (LOE).

attributes.name: sla_terms
attributes.description: Full text or reference to the Service Level Agreement (SLA) terms applicable to this tier, including response times, escalation procedures, and performance guarantees. Used in engagement letters (LOE) and client contracts.

attributes.name: tier_code
attributes.description: Short alphanumeric code uniquely identifying the service tier (e.g., STD, PREM, ENT, BESPOKE). Used in system integrations and billing configurations.

attributes.name: tier_description
attributes.description: Detailed description of the service tier, including scope of coverage, key differentiators, and target client segments. Used in business development materials and RFP responses.

attributes.name: tier_level
attributes.description: Numeric ranking of the tier within the service hierarchy (e.g., 1=Standard, 2=Premium, 3=Enterprise, 4=Bespoke). Used for sorting and eligibility logic.

attributes.name: tier_name
attributes.description: Full business name of the service tier (e.g., Standard, Premium, Enterprise, Bespoke). Used in client-facing documents, RFPs, and engagement letters (LOE).

attributes.name: tier_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the service tier. Active tiers are available for new engagements; deprecated tiers are honored for existing matters but not offered to new clients.

attributes.name: version_number
attributes.description: Version number of this service tier configuration. Incremented with each substantive change to tier terms, pricing, or scope. Used in change management and historical analysis.

products.name: pricing_model
products.description: Defines the fee structures and alternative fee arrangements (AFA) applicable to legal service offerings, including hourly billing, fixed fee, capped fee, blended rate, retainer, contingency, and success fee models. Each record captures the model type, calculation basis, currency, applicable jurisdictions, and LEDES/UTBMS billing code alignment. Serves as the authoritative pricing configuration referenced by billing and matter domains.

attributes.name: pricing_model_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the pricing model record. Primary key.

attributes.name: attorney_profile_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the partner who approved this pricing model for use. Null if not yet approved or approval not required.

attributes.name: category_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to risk.risk_category. Business justification: AFA pricing models require risk classification (contingency = outcome risk, fixed fee = scope risk, capped fee = budget overrun risk). Pricing committees evaluate risk category before approving non-st

attributes.name: legal_service_id
attributes.description: FK to service.legal_service.legal_service_id — Pricing models are configured per legal service offering. Each service has one or more applicable pricing models (hourly, fixed, capped, etc.).

attributes.name: segment_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to client.client_segment. Business justification: Pricing models are often segment-specific (volume discounts for enterprise clients, standard rates for individuals). Rate cards, AFA eligibility, and discount structures are determined by client segme

attributes.name: advance_payment_amount
attributes.description: Required advance payment or retainer deposit amount. Null if no advance payment is required.
attributes.references: Elite 3E Retainer Management; IOLTA Trust Account Rules

attributes.name: advance_payment_required
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether an advance payment or retainer deposit is required before work commences under this pricing model. True = advance required; False = no advance.
attributes.references: Elite 3E Retainer Management; IOLTA Trust Account Rules

attributes.name: afa_indicator
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether this pricing model represents an Alternative Fee Arrangement (non-traditional hourly billing). True = AFA; False = traditional hourly.
attributes.references: ABA Commission on Billable Hours Report

attributes.name: applicable_jurisdictions
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of jurisdictions where this pricing model is approved for use (e.g., 'USA, GBR, CAN'). Ensures compliance with local bar association fee rules.
attributes.references: State Bar Associations; Law Society of England and Wales; Solicitors Regulation Authority

attributes.name: applicable_practice_areas
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of practice areas where this pricing model is typically applied (e.g., 'M&A, Corporate Transactions', 'Litigation, Dispute Resolution'). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: litigation|corporate|ip|employment|regulatory|real_estate|tax|bankruptcy|family|immigration — promote to reference product]

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: Date on which this pricing model was approved by authorized partner or management. Null if not yet approved.

attributes.name: approval_required
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether partner or management approval is required before applying this pricing model to a matter. True = approval required; False = no approval needed.

attributes.name: base_rate_amount
attributes.description: The standard rate amount for this pricing model. For hourly models, this is the hourly rate; for fixed fee, this is the base fee amount. Null if rate varies by timekeeper or matter.
attributes.references: Elite 3E Rate Management; Aderant Expert Rate Tables

attributes.name: billing_increment_minutes
attributes.description: Time increment used for rounding billable time entries (e.g., 6 minutes = 0.1 hour, 15 minutes = 0.25 hour). Common values: 6, 10, 15.
attributes.references: Elite 3E Time Entry; Aderant Expert Timekeeper Management

attributes.name: blended_rate_amount
attributes.description: Single averaged hourly rate applied across all timekeepers on a matter, regardless of individual seniority. Used in blended rate pricing models.
attributes.references: Elite 3E Rate Management; Aderant Expert Rate Tables

attributes.name: calculation_basis
attributes.description: The foundational method used to calculate fees under this model. Time-based = hours worked; Matter-based = per matter/case; Transaction Value = percentage of deal value; Outcome-based = tied to result; Hybrid = combination of methods.

attributes.name: contingency_percentage
attributes.description: The percentage of recovery or transaction value that constitutes the fee for contingency-based pricing models. Null for non-contingency models.
attributes.references: ABA Model Rules of Professional Conduct Rule 1.5(c)

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this pricing model record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: discount_percentage
attributes.description: Standard discount percentage applied to standard rates under this pricing model. Null if no discount applies.

attributes.name: effective_end_date
attributes.description: Date on which this pricing model expires or is no longer available for new matters. Null for open-ended models.
attributes.references: Elite 3E Rate Management; Aderant Expert Rate Tables

attributes.name: effective_start_date
attributes.description: Date from which this pricing model becomes effective and available for use in client engagements.
attributes.references: Elite 3E Rate Management; Aderant Expert Rate Tables

attributes.name: expense_markup_percentage
attributes.description: Percentage markup applied to reimbursable expenses (e.g., 10% administrative fee on disbursements). Null if no markup applies.

attributes.name: expense_reimbursement_policy
attributes.description: Policy governing how disbursements and expenses are handled under this pricing model. Full = all expenses billed separately; Capped = expenses up to limit; Included = expenses absorbed in fee; No Reimbursement = client pays directly.
attributes.references: ABA Model Rules of Professional Conduct Rule 1.5; Elite 3E Disbursement Management

attributes.name: internal_notes
attributes.description: Internal notes and comments about this pricing model for firm use only. May include strategic considerations, client negotiation history, or profitability analysis.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this pricing model record was last updated.

attributes.name: late_payment_interest_rate
attributes.description: Annual interest rate applied to overdue invoices under this pricing model. Null if no late payment interest applies.
attributes.references: ABA Model Rules of Professional Conduct Rule 1.5; Jurisdiction-specific Interest Statutes

attributes.name: ledes_format_version
attributes.business_glossary_term: Legal Electronic Data Exchange Standard (LEDES) Format Version
attributes.description: LEDES billing format version supported by this pricing model (e.g., LEDES1998BI, LEDES1998BIV2). Ensures billing data compatibility with client systems.

attributes.name: maximum_fee_amount
attributes.description: The maximum fee cap for capped fee arrangements. Fees will not exceed this amount regardless of time spent. Null if no cap applies.
attributes.references: ABA Model Rules of Professional Conduct Rule 1.5

attributes.name: minimum_fee_amount
attributes.description: The minimum fee that will be charged under this pricing model, regardless of time or effort expended. Null if no minimum applies.
attributes.references: ABA Model Rules of Professional Conduct Rule 1.5

attributes.name: model_code
attributes.description: Business identifier code for the pricing model, used in billing systems and client communications.

attributes.name: model_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name of the pricing model (e.g., 'Standard Hourly Billing', 'Fixed Fee M&A Advisory', 'Blended Rate Litigation').

attributes.name: model_type
attributes.description: Classification of the fee structure type. Hourly = time-based billing; Fixed Fee = predetermined amount; Capped Fee = hourly with maximum limit; Blended Rate = averaged rate across timekeepers; Retainer = recurring periodic fee; Contingency = success-based percentage.
attributes.references: ABA Model Rules of Professional Conduct Rule 1.5; LEDES Billing Code Standard

attributes.name: payment_terms_days
attributes.description: Standard payment terms in days from invoice date (e.g., 30 days net). Defines when payment is due under this pricing model.
attributes.references: Elite 3E Accounts Receivable; Client Engagement Letters

attributes.name: pricing_model_description
attributes.description: Detailed description of the pricing model, including its intended use cases, calculation methodology, and any special terms or conditions.

attributes.name: pricing_model_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the pricing model. Active = in use; Inactive = not available for new matters; Draft = under development; Archived = historical; Under Review = pending approval; Approved = ready for activation.

attributes.name: rate_currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the rate amount (e.g., USD, GBP, EUR).

attributes.name: retainer_amount
attributes.description: The recurring retainer fee amount charged per billing period. Null for non-retainer models.

attributes.name: retainer_frequency
attributes.description: Billing frequency for retainer-based pricing models. Indicates how often the retainer fee is charged.

attributes.name: sla_resolution_time_days
attributes.description: Target resolution or delivery time in days for matters under this pricing model. Part of service level commitments.

attributes.name: sla_response_time_hours
attributes.description: Guaranteed response time in hours for client inquiries under this pricing model. Part of service level commitments.

attributes.name: success_fee_amount
attributes.description: Fixed or additional fee payable upon successful outcome (e.g., case won, deal closed). Null if no success fee applies.
attributes.references: ABA Model Rules of Professional Conduct Rule 1.5

attributes.name: utbms_task_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: Uniform Task-Based Management System (UTBMS) Task Code
attributes.description: UTBMS task code alignment for this pricing model, enabling standardized billing code reporting (e.g., L110 for Case Assessment, L310 for Discovery).
attributes.references: UTBMS Task-Based Management System; LEDES Billing Standard

attributes.name: last_modified_by_user_timekeeper_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the user who last modified this pricing model record.

products.name: rate_card
products.description: Stores the standard and negotiated timekeeper billing rates for legal services by practice area, seniority level (partner, associate, paralegal), jurisdiction, and client segment. Captures effective date ranges, currency, rate type (standard, preferred, blended), and UTBMS task code alignment. Feeds directly into Elite 3E and Aderant Expert rate management modules for WIP calculation and prebilling. Distinct from pricing_model which defines the fee structure type.

attributes.name: rate_card_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the rate card record. Primary key.

attributes.name: matter_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific matter for which this rate applies. Null indicates the rate applies at the client level or as a standard rate.

attributes.name: profile_id
attributes.description: Reference to the client for whom this rate is defined. Null indicates a standard rate applicable to all clients unless overridden.

attributes.name: superseded_by_rate_card_id
attributes.description: Reference to the rate card that supersedes this one. Null if this is the current active rate card.

attributes.name: timekeeper_id
attributes.description: Reference to the timekeeper (attorney, paralegal, or other legal professional) to whom this rate applies.

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: Date on which this rate card was approved for use.

attributes.name: approval_status
attributes.description: Current approval status of the rate card in the rate management workflow (draft = under construction, pending_approval = submitted for review, approved = active and usable, rejected = not approved, expired = past effective end date).

attributes.name: approved_by
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the individual who approved this rate card (typically a partner, billing manager, or finance director).

attributes.name: billing_guideline_compliant
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this rate complies with the client's outside counsel billing guidelines (True = compliant, False = non-compliant or requires review).

attributes.name: client_segment
attributes.description: Classification of the client segment to which this rate applies (e.g., Fortune 500, mid-market, small business, government, non-profit, individual).

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this rate card record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code in which the rate is denominated (e.g., USD, GBP, EUR, JPY).

attributes.name: discount_percentage
attributes.description: Percentage discount applied to the standard rate to derive this rate (e.g., 10.00 for a 10% discount). Null if no discount applies.

attributes.name: effective_end_date
attributes.description: The date on which this rate ceases to be effective. Null indicates the rate is currently active with no defined end date.

attributes.name: effective_start_date
attributes.description: The date from which this rate becomes effective and applicable for billing purposes.

attributes.name: hourly_rate
attributes.description: The billing rate per hour for the timekeeper's services under this rate card. Used for time-based billing calculations in Elite 3E and Aderant Expert.
attributes.references: Elite 3E Rate Management, Aderant Expert Prebilling

attributes.name: is_active
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this rate card is currently active and available for use in billing (True = active, False = inactive).

attributes.name: is_default_rate
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this is the default rate to be applied when no client-specific or matter-specific rate is defined (True = default, False = not default).

attributes.name: jurisdiction_code
attributes.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code or state/province code representing the jurisdiction where the legal services are provided (e.g., USA, GBR, NY, CA).

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this rate card record was last updated or modified.

attributes.name: minimum_charge_increment_minutes
attributes.description: Minimum time increment for billing purposes (e.g., 6 minutes for 0.1 hour increments, 15 minutes for 0.25 hour increments). Used in time entry rounding.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes or comments regarding this rate card, including special terms, exceptions, or context for the rate structure.

attributes.name: rate_cap_amount
attributes.description: Maximum hourly rate cap agreed with the client, regardless of timekeeper seniority or standard rate. Null if no cap applies.

attributes.name: rate_card_description
attributes.description: Detailed description of the rate card, including its purpose, scope, and any special terms or conditions.

attributes.name: rate_card_name
attributes.description: Descriptive name or label for this rate card (e.g., '2024 Standard Corporate Rates', 'Client XYZ Preferred Rates', 'Litigation Blended Rate').

attributes.name: rate_floor_amount
attributes.description: Minimum hourly rate floor below which billing cannot fall. Null if no floor applies.

attributes.name: rate_source
attributes.description: Origin or basis for this rate (firm_standard = firm's published standard rates, client_negotiated = negotiated with client, engagement_letter = specified in Letter of Engagement (LOE), rfp_response = proposed in RFP response, afa_agreement = part of Alternative Fee Arrangement, market_benchmark = based on market survey).

attributes.name: rate_type
attributes.description: Classification of the billing rate structure (standard = firm standard rate, preferred = client-specific preferred rate, blended = averaged rate across multiple timekeepers, discounted = reduced rate, negotiated = custom negotiated rate, afa = Alternative Fee Arrangement rate).

attributes.name: rate_version
attributes.description: Version number of this rate card, incremented with each revision or update. Used for rate history tracking and audit purposes.

attributes.name: seniority_level
attributes.description: Seniority classification of the timekeeper (e.g., equity partner, non-equity partner, of counsel, senior associate, mid-level associate, junior associate, paralegal, legal assistant, contract attorney). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: equity_partner|non_equity_partner|of_counsel|senior_associate|mid_level_associate|junior_associate|paralegal|legal_assistant|contract_attorney — 9 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: utbms_activity_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: Uniform Task-Based Management System (UTBMS) Activity Code
attributes.description: UTBMS activity code providing granular detail on the type of legal work performed under this rate (e.g., A101 for Plan and Prepare for Issue Development).

attributes.name: utbms_task_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: Uniform Task-Based Management System (UTBMS) Task Code
attributes.description: UTBMS task code aligned with this rate for standardized legal billing and matter management (e.g., L110 for Case Assessment, L120 for Investigation).

attributes.name: rate_practice_area_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to service.practice_area. Business justification: Rate cards are scoped by practice area. Normalize by linking to practice_area master. Remove practice_area_name as it can be retrieved via JOIN to practice_area.name.

attributes.name: office_location_code
attributes.description: Code representing the office location from which the timekeeper operates (e.g., NYC, LON, SFO, HKG).

products.name: sla_template

Used in LOE drafting, RFP responses, and matter management SLA monitoring. Distinct from individual matter-level SLA instances.

attributes.name: sla_template_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the SLA template. Primary key.

attributes.name: legal_service_id

attributes.name: offering_version_id
attributes.description: Reference to the legal service offering catalog entry to which this SLA template is associated.

attributes.name: practice_area_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to service.practice_area. Business justification: SLA templates are scoped by practice area. Normalize by linking to practice_area master. The practice_area STRING column is a code/name reference.

attributes.name: pricing_model_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to service.pricing_model. Business justification: SLA templates may reference a pricing model. Normalize by linking to pricing_model master. The pricing_model STRING column is a code/name reference.

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: Date on which this SLA template was formally approved for use in client engagements.

attributes.name: approval_status
attributes.description: Current approval and lifecycle status of the SLA template within the firm's governance process.

attributes.name: approved_by
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the partner or practice group leader who approved this SLA template for use.

attributes.name: availability_commitment
attributes.description: Timekeeper availability commitment specified in the SLA (e.g., 24/7 emergency access, business hours only, named partner availability).

attributes.name: breach_count
attributes.description: Historical count of SLA breaches across all matters using this template, used for template refinement and risk assessment.

attributes.name: breach_threshold_percentage

attributes.name: client_tier
attributes.description: Client segmentation tier for which this SLA template is designed, reflecting service level differentiation in client relationship management.

attributes.name: communication_protocol

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this SLA template record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date from which this SLA template becomes effective and available for use in new Letter of Engagement (LOE) drafting and matter setup.

attributes.name: escalation_threshold
attributes.description: Threshold value (in same unit as response/turnaround time) at which SLA breach triggers escalation to senior counsel or practice group leader.

attributes.name: escalation_unit

attributes.name: expiration_date
attributes.description: Date on which this SLA template expires or is superseded by a newer version. Null indicates no expiration.

attributes.name: fee_adjustment_percentage
attributes.description: Percentage fee adjustment (reduction or credit) applied upon SLA breach as specified in remediation terms.

attributes.name: jurisdiction
attributes.description: Legal jurisdiction or geographic scope to which this SLA template applies (e.g., USA, GBR, multi-jurisdictional). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: USA|GBR|CAN|AUS|DEU|FRA|CHN|IND|multi_jurisdictional — promote to reference product]

attributes.name: matter_complexity
attributes.description: Target matter complexity level for which this SLA template is appropriate, enabling proper SLA-to-matter matching.

attributes.name: modified_by
attributes.description: Identifier of the user or system that last modified this SLA template record.

attributes.name: modified_timestamp

products.name: eligibility_rule
products.description: Defines configurable business rules governing which clients or matters qualify for specific legal service offerings during new business intake. Rule types include client-type restrictions (corporate, government, individual), minimum matter value thresholds, jurisdictional licensing constraints, industry sector exclusions, and prerequisite clearance requirements. Each rule specifies evaluation logic, enforcement level (hard block preventing engagement vs. advisory warning requiring partner override), and the legal_service scope to which it applies. Consumed by the intake workflow engine during RFP qualification and matter opening. products.name: delivery_configuration
products.description: This association product represents the operational configuration between legal services and delivery models. It captures which services can be delivered through which models, tracking effectiveness, cost allocation, and SLA overrides for each combination. Each record links one legal_service to one delivery_model with attributes that exist only in the context of this specific service-model pairing, used in capacity planning, RFP staffing proposals, and client delivery optimization.. Existence Justification: In legal services operations, firms actively manage which services can be delivered through which delivery models, creating a genuine many-to-many operational relationship. A single legal service (e.g., M&A advisory) can be delivered through multiple models (traditional partner-led, ALSP co-delivery, managed legal services) depending on client requirements, matter complexity, and cost constraints. Conversely, a single delivery model (e.g., client secondment) can be used to deliver multiple different legal services (litigation, IP counsel, regulatory compliance). The firm tracks the effectiveness, cost allocation, and SLA commitments for each specific service-model pairing.

products.name: practice_area_delivery_configuration
products.description: This association product represents the operational configuration between practice areas and delivery models in legal service delivery. It captures which practice areas can be delivered through which delivery models, along with capacity allocation, performance targets, and effectiveness tracking. Each record links one practice area to one delivery model with attributes that define the operational parameters, resource allocation, and quality metrics for that specific combination. This is actively managed by legal operations teams for capacity planning, RFP response preparation, and delivery optimization.. Existence Justification: In legal operations, practice areas can be delivered through multiple delivery models (e.g., M&A can be delivered via traditional partner-led teams, ALSP co-delivery, or managed legal services), and each delivery model supports multiple practice areas (e.g., ALSP co-delivery can handle IP, employment law, and regulatory compliance). Legal operations teams actively manage this matrix to allocate capacity, respond to RFPs with appropriate staffing models, track delivery effectiveness, and optimize resource deployment across the practice-delivery configuration space.

Captures practice area, matter type, service description, geographic scope, included and excluded services, staffing plan (partner, associate, paralegal), estimated hours by role, and scope version number. Serves as the commercial specification that feeds the LOE drafting process and AFA negotiation. Linked to the engagement opportunity and the resulting letter of engagement. Owned by the intake domain as the pre-matter scope definition.

attributes.description: Unique identifier for the engagement scope record. Primary key for the intake engagement scope entity.

attributes.name: approved_date
attributes.description: Date when the engagement scope was formally approved by the lead partner or practice group head. Triggers LOE drafting process.

attributes.name: client_responsibilities
attributes.description: Explicit list of responsibilities, actions, or deliverables expected from the client to enable successful engagement execution (e.g., document provision, decision-making, access to personnel).
attributes.references: ABA Model Rules of Professional Conduct - Rule 1.2 (Scope of Representation)

attributes.name: conflict_check_reference
attributes.description: Reference number or identifier for the conflict check record in Intapp Conflicts system associated with this engagement scope.

attributes.name: conflict_check_status
attributes.description: Status of the conflict check process for this engagement scope. Must be cleared before LOE execution. Values: pending (check in progress), cleared (no conflicts), conditional (cleared with ethical walls), declined (conflict identified).
attributes.references: ABA Model Rules of Professional Conduct - Rule 1.7 (Conflict of Interest)

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the engagement scope record was first created in the intake system. Marks the beginning of scope definition activity.

attributes.name: engagement_duration_months
attributes.description: Estimated duration of the engagement in months. Used for resource planning and AFA structuring. Null for open-ended or event-driven engagements.

attributes.name: estimated_completion_date

attributes.name: estimated_start_date

attributes.name: estimated_total_hours
attributes.description: Total estimated hours across all timekeeper roles for the engagement. Sum of partner, associate, paralegal, and other staff hours. Used for capacity planning and fee estimation.

attributes.name: excluded_services
attributes.description: Explicit list of services, tasks, and activities that are outside the agreed engagement scope. Critical for scope management and preventing scope creep.
attributes.references: ABA Model Rules of Professional Conduct - Rule 1.2 (Scope of Representation)

attributes.name: geographic_scope
attributes.description: Geographic jurisdictions, countries, or regions covered by the engagement scope. Relevant for multi-jurisdictional matters and cross-border transactions.

attributes.name: included_services
attributes.description: Explicit list of services, tasks, and deliverables that are included within the agreed engagement scope. Used to define boundaries and manage client expectations.

products.name: intake_fee_arrangement
products.description: Master record capturing the negotiated fee arrangement (AFA) agreed with a prospective client during the intake and engagement scoping process. Tracks AFA type (hourly, fixed fee, capped fee, contingency, blended rate, retainer, success fee), agreed fee amount or rate schedule reference, billing frequency, currency, discount applied, approval status, approving partner, and effective date. Linked to the engagement scope and letter of engagement. Sourced from Elite 3E rate and billing configuration. Distinct from the billing domains rate schedule — this entity captures the negotiated commercial agreement, not the rate table.

attributes.description: Reference to the partner who approved this fee arrangement. Ensures appropriate authority and risk oversight for non-standard or discounted fee structures.

attributes.description: Reference to the engagement scope that this fee arrangement supports. Links the commercial agreement to the defined scope of legal services.

attributes.name: engagement_opportunity_id

attributes.name: profile_id
attributes.description: Reference to the prospective client for whom this fee arrangement is being negotiated during intake.

attributes.name: request_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to intake.intake_request. Business justification: Fee arrangements are negotiated during the intake workflow. Linking to intake_request provides workflow traceability from fee arrangement back to the originating intake request. This is a standard par

attributes.name: agreed_fee_amount
attributes.description: The total fee amount agreed for fixed fee, capped fee, or retainer arrangements. Null for hourly or contingency arrangements where the amount is variable. Represents the commercial commitment in the engagement.

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: The date on which the fee arrangement was formally approved by the approving partner. Marks the transition from proposed to approved status.

attributes.name: arrangement_number
attributes.description: Business identifier for the fee arrangement, typically generated during intake negotiation. Used for tracking and reference in proposals and letters of engagement.

attributes.name: arrangement_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the fee arrangement. Tracks progression from initial draft through negotiation to final approval or rejection. Superseded indicates a revised arrangement has replaced this one.

attributes.name: billing_fee_arrangement_id
attributes.description: Foreign key to billing.fee_arrangement.fee_arrangement_id

attributes.name: billing_frequency
attributes.description: The agreed frequency at which invoices will be issued to the client. Monthly and quarterly are common for ongoing matters; milestone and completion are typical for project-based work; on-demand for ad-hoc arrangements.

attributes.name: blended_rate
attributes.description: The single averaged hourly rate applied across all timekeepers for blended rate arrangements. Simplifies billing by eliminating individual rate variations. Null for non-blended arrangements.

attributes.name: cap_amount
attributes.description: The maximum fee amount that can be billed for capped fee arrangements. Provides cost certainty to the client while allowing hourly billing up to the cap. Null for non-capped arrangements.

attributes.name: contingency_percentage
attributes.description: The percentage of recovery or settlement that the firm will receive as its fee in contingency arrangements. Typically ranges from 10% to 40% depending on jurisdiction and matter type. Null for non-contingency arrangements.
attributes.references: American Bar Association (ABA) Model Rules of Professional Conduct Rule 1.5

attributes.name: created_by_user
attributes.description: The username or identifier of the user who created this fee arrangement record. Typically a business development professional, partner, or pricing analyst involved in the intake process.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this fee arrangement record was first created in the source system. Represents the start of the fee arrangement negotiation lifecycle.

attributes.name: disbursement_handling
attributes.description: Defines how disbursements (out-of-pocket expenses such as court fees, filing fees, expert fees) are treated in the fee arrangement. Included means absorbed in the fixed fee; pass-through means billed at cost; marked-up means billed with an administrative margin.

attributes.name: discount_percentage
attributes.description: The percentage discount applied to standard rates as part of the negotiated fee arrangement. Common in competitive pitches or for high-volume clients. Zero if no discount applied.

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: The date from which this fee arrangement becomes active and governs billing for the engagement. Typically aligns with the letter of engagement execution date.

attributes.name: expiry_date
attributes.description: The date on which this fee arrangement expires or terminates. Null for open-ended arrangements. Used for time-limited retainers or project-based fixed fees.

attributes.name: is_outside_counsel_guideline_compliant
attributes.description: Indicates whether this fee arrangement complies with the client's outside counsel guidelines. Many corporate clients impose billing guidelines that restrict rate increases, require task-based billing codes (UTBMS), and mandate electronic invoicing (LEDES).
attributes.references: Uniform Task-Based Management System (UTBMS), Legal Electronic Data Exchange Standard (LEDES)

attributes.name: ledes_format_required
attributes.business_glossary_term: Legal Electronic Data Exchange Standard (LEDES) Format Required Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether invoices under this fee arrangement must be submitted in LEDES electronic format. LEDES is the industry standard for electronic billing data exchange between law firms and corporate clients.

attributes.name: loe_reference
attributes.description: Reference number or identifier of the letter of engagement that formalizes this fee arrangement. Links the commercial agreement to the binding engagement contract.

attributes.name: minimum_fee_commitment
attributes.description: The minimum total fee the client commits to pay over a defined period, regardless of actual work performed. Common in retainer and volume-based arrangements to guarantee revenue. Null if no minimum applies.

attributes.name: modified_by_user
attributes.description: The username or identifier of the user who last modified this fee arrangement record. Tracks accountability for changes during negotiation and approval.

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this fee arrangement record was last modified in the source system. Tracks changes during negotiation and approval cycles.

attributes.name: negotiation_notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes capturing key points from fee negotiation discussions, client concerns, competitive pressures, and rationale for the final agreed terms. Supports knowledge management and future client interactions.

attributes.name: payment_terms_days
attributes.description: Number of days from invoice date within which payment is due. Standard terms are 30 days, but may be negotiated to 14, 60, or other periods based on client relationship and creditworthiness.

attributes.name: rate_schedule_reference
attributes.description: Reference to the rate schedule or rate card that underpins this fee arrangement. Links to the firm's rate table in Elite 3E. Used for hourly and blended rate arrangements to track the base rates before discounts.

attributes.name: rejection_reason
attributes.description: Explanation for why the fee arrangement was rejected, either by the client or by internal approval authority. Captures business intelligence for future pricing and negotiation strategies. Null if not rejected.

attributes.name: retainer_period
attributes.description: The recurring period for retainer fee arrangements. Defines how frequently the retainer fee is charged (e.g., monthly retainer for ongoing advisory services). Null for non-retainer arrangements.

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: The operational system from which this fee arrangement record was sourced. Typically Elite 3E rate and billing configuration or Microsoft Dynamics 365 CRM during the intake pipeline stage.

attributes.name: source_system_code
attributes.description: The unique identifier of this fee arrangement in the source system (e.g., Elite 3E fee arrangement ID). Enables traceability and reconciliation between the lakehouse and operational systems.

attributes.name: success_criteria_description
attributes.description: Detailed description of the conditions that must be met to trigger the success fee. Defines measurable outcomes such as settlement amount thresholds, deal completion, or favorable court rulings.

attributes.name: success_fee_amount
attributes.description: Additional fee payable upon achieving defined success criteria (e.g., favorable judgment, transaction close, regulatory approval). Common in M&A, litigation, and regulatory matters. Null if no success fee applies.
attributes.references: Solicitors Regulation Authority (SRA) Standards and Regulations

attributes.name: utbms_task_code_required
attributes.business_glossary_term: Uniform Task-Based Management System (UTBMS) Task Code Required Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether time entries under this fee arrangement must be coded using UTBMS task codes for billing compliance. Required by many corporate clients for invoice transparency and spend analytics.

products.name: letter_of_engagement
products.description: Master record representing the Letter of Engagement (LOE) issued to a prospective client formalizing the attorney-client relationship, scope of services, fee arrangement, and terms of engagement. Tracks LOE version, issue date, acceptance date, signatory details, governing law, jurisdiction, LPP acknowledgment, data protection consent (GDPR/DPA), conflict waiver references, and execution status (draft, issued, accepted, declined, superseded). The LOE execution event triggers the handoff from the intake domain to the matter domain for matter opening in Elite 3E. Owned by the intake domain as the pre-matter commercial instrument.

products.name: risk_action
products.description: This association product represents the assignment of risk mitigation actions to specific intake requests in the new business intake lifecycle. It captures the operational linkage between intake requests that trigger risk concerns (conflicts, sanctions, reputational issues) and the specific mitigation actions assigned to address those concerns. Each record links one intake request to one risk mitigation action with attributes that track the assignment context, timing, priority, effort, and completion status specific to that intake-action pairing.. Existence Justification: In legal firm intake operations, a single intake request can trigger multiple distinct risk mitigation actions (conflict waiver, enhanced KYC, sanctions clearance, ethical wall implementation, reputational review) based on the specific risk profile of the proposed matter. Conversely, a single mitigation action template (e.g., implementing an ethical wall protocol) can be assigned to address risks identified across multiple concurrent intake requests involving related parties or overlapping conflicts. The business actively manages these assignments as operational records with timing, priority, and completion tracking specific to each intake-action pairing.

attributes.name: action_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of this mitigation action in the context of this specific intake request. Tracks progression from assignment through completion.

attributes.name: actual_effort_hours

attributes.name: assigned_date

attributes.name: estimated_effort_hours

products.name: opportunity_risk_assessment
products.description: This association product represents the formal risk evaluation performed for a specific engagement opportunity during the business development lifecycle. It captures the point-in-time risk assessment conducted as part of client acceptance, conflict clearance, and engagement approval processes. Each record links one engagement opportunity to one risk assessment with attributes that exist only in the context of this evaluation relationship.. Existence Justification: In legal services business development, engagement opportunities undergo multiple formal risk assessments at different stages of the pipeline (initial screening at qualification, detailed due diligence during proposal, pre-engagement final review before LOE execution). A single comprehensive risk assessment can also evaluate multiple related opportunities simultaneously (e.g., panel appointment covering multiple anticipated matters, multi-jurisdiction engagement with separate opportunity records). The business actively manages these assessment relationships with stage-specific scores, approval workflows, and reviewer assignments.

Covers professional indemnity exposure, data breach incident management (PII/GDPR), cybersecurity risk (ISO 27001), sanctions screening, and reputational risk flags. Provides the risk register that feeds compliance, conflict, and workforce domains without duplicating their operational data.

products.name: register
products.description: Enterprise-wide and matter-level risk register serving as the authoritative single source of truth for all identified risks across professional indemnity, data breach, cybersecurity, sanctions, reputational, and operational categories. Each record represents a discrete risk item with classification, inherent and residual risk ratings (likelihood × impact matrix), current mitigation status, risk owner, escalation history, exception status (approved deviations from policy with approval metadata), and review cycle scheduling. Supports Risk Committee reporting, SRA regulatory submissions, ISO 31000 alignment, and feeds compliance, conflict, and workforce domains.

attributes.name: exception_approved_by
