attributes.name: exception_expiry_date
attributes.description: The date on which the approved policy exception expires and must be re-evaluated or revoked. Null if no exception is in force. Drives exception renewal alerts.

attributes.name: identified_date
attributes.description: The calendar date on which this risk was first identified and logged in the risk register. Serves as the principal business event date for the risk lifecycle and is used in ageing analysis.

attributes.name: inherent_impact
attributes.description: Impact rating of the risk materialising before any controls are applied, scored on a 1–5 scale (1=Negligible, 2=Minor, 3=Moderate, 4=Major, 5=Catastrophic). Combined with inherent_likelihood to produce the inherent risk rating.

attributes.name: inherent_likelihood
attributes.description: Likelihood rating of the risk occurring before any controls are applied, scored on a 1–5 scale (1=Rare, 2=Unlikely, 3=Possible, 4=Likely, 5=Almost Certain) per the firm's risk appetite matrix. Used to compute the inherent risk rating.

attributes.name: inherent_risk_rating
attributes.description: Pre-control risk score calculated as inherent_likelihood × inherent_impact (range 1–25). Represents the gross risk exposure before mitigation. Used to prioritise risk treatment and populate the firm's risk heat map.

attributes.name: insurance_claim_ref
attributes.description: Reference number of the professional indemnity insurance claim raised with the firm's insurer in relation to this risk event. Populated when a claim has been formally notified to the insurer. Classified confidential.
attributes.references: SRA Indemnity Insurance Rules; ABA Model Rules; ISO 31000:2018

attributes.name: is_exception_approved
attributes.description: Indicates whether a formal policy exception has been approved for this risk, permitting a deviation from the firm's standard risk management policy. True when an approved exception is in force.
attributes.references: ISO 31000:2018; SRA Code of Conduct; ISO 27001:2022

attributes.name: last_reviewed_date

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp

attributes.name: lpp_applies

attributes.name: mitigation_description

attributes.name: mitigation_status

attributes.name: next_review_date

attributes.name: pii_involved

attributes.name: regulatory_body

attributes.name: regulatory_notification_date

attributes.name: regulatory_reporting_required

attributes.name: residual_impact

attributes.name: residual_likelihood

attributes.name: residual_risk_rating

attributes.name: risk_domain

attributes.name: risk_ref_code

attributes.references: ISO 31000:2018; SRA Code of Conduct; ABA Model Rules

attributes.name: category_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of this risk category within the firm's taxonomy. 'Active' categories are available for use in risk register entries; 'deprecated' categories are retained for historical reporting only; 'under_review' categories are pending approval for modification.

attributes.name: control_framework_reference
attributes.description: Reference to the specific control framework, standard, or policy document that governs the mitigating controls applicable to this risk category (e.g., 'ISO 27001 Annex A', 'GDPR Article 32 Technical Measures', 'SRA AML Policy', 'FATF Recommendation 10'). Enables traceability from risk category to control library.
attributes.references: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A; GDPR Article 32; FATF Recommendations; SRA AML Guidance

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time at which this risk category record was first created in the enterprise risk taxonomy. Provides the audit trail entry point for taxonomy governance and change management.

attributes.name: cybersecurity_relevance_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this risk category falls within the scope of the firm's ISO 27001 Information Security Management System (ISMS). When true, associated risks are subject to ISO 27001 Annex A control requirements and must be included in the Statement of Applicability.

attributes.name: effective_from_date
attributes.description: Date from which this risk category became or becomes effective within the firm's risk taxonomy. Supports temporal validity tracking and ensures risk register entries are only associated with categories that were active at the time of the risk event.

attributes.name: effective_to_date
attributes.description: Date on which this risk category ceases to be effective within the firm's risk taxonomy. Null for currently active categories. Enables point-in-time risk reporting and historical taxonomy reconstruction.

attributes.name: escalation_level
attributes.description: Minimum organisational level to which risk incidents under this category must be escalated when the residual risk score exceeds the appetite threshold. Drives automated escalation routing in the risk management workflow.
attributes.references: ISO 31000:2018; SRA Code of Conduct; ABA Model Rules Rule 5.1

attributes.name: external_reference_code
attributes.description: External standard or regulatory reference code that maps this risk category to an industry-standard taxonomy (e.g., ISO 31000 risk category code, COSO ERM category, SRA Risk Outlook category code). Supports benchmarking and regulatory reporting alignment.
attributes.references: ISO 31000:2018; COSO ERM Framework; SRA Risk Outlook

attributes.name: governing_body
attributes.description: Name of the primary regulatory or professional body whose rules or standards give rise to this risk category (e.g., 'Solicitors Regulation Authority', 'American Bar Association', 'Financial Action Task Force', 'Information Commissioner's Office'). Supports jurisdiction-specific risk reporting.
attributes.references: SRA; ABA; IBA; Legal Services Board; FATF; ISO

attributes.name: hierarchy_level
attributes.description: Numeric depth of this category within the risk taxonomy hierarchy. Level 1 represents top-level domains; higher values represent increasingly granular sub-categories. Supports hierarchical roll-up in risk dashboards and regulatory reports.

attributes.name: hierarchy_path
attributes.description: Delimited string representing the full ancestry path of the risk category within the taxonomy (e.g., 'Regulatory Risk > Data Privacy > PII/GDPR'). Facilitates breadcrumb navigation and hierarchical filtering in risk reporting tools.

attributes.name: inherent_risk_score
attributes.description: Numeric composite score representing the firm's inherent (pre-control) exposure for this risk category, calculated as the product of likelihood and impact ratings on the firm's standard risk matrix. Provides a baseline for risk prioritisation before mitigating controls are applied.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time at which this risk category record was most recently updated. Supports change tracking, data lineage, and audit trail requirements for the Silver Layer lakehouse.

attributes.name: last_reviewed_by
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the risk owner, partner, or committee member who last formally reviewed and approved this risk category. Supports accountability and audit trail requirements under the firm's risk governance framework.
attributes.references: ISO 31000:2018; SRA Code of Conduct; ABA Model Rules Rule 5.1

attributes.name: last_reviewed_date
attributes.description: Date on which this risk category definition was most recently formally reviewed and approved by the Risk Committee or designated risk owner. Provides an audit trail for taxonomy governance.

attributes.name: lpp_relevance_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this risk category involves matters that may engage Legal Professional Privilege (LPP), requiring special handling protocols to preserve privilege and avoid inadvertent waiver. Relevant for litigation, regulatory investigation, and eDiscovery risk categories.
attributes.references: ABA Model Rules of Professional Conduct Rule 1.6; Law Society of England and Wales – LPP Guidance

attributes.name: matter_type_applicability
attributes.description: Comma-separated list or description of the matter types or practice areas to which this risk category is most applicable (e.g., 'Litigation, Arbitration', 'M&A, Corporate Transactions', 'IP Portfolio Management', 'All Matters'). Guides risk assessment scoping during matter intake.
attributes.references: ABA Model Rules; SRA Code of Conduct; Elite 3E Matter Management

attributes.name: next_review_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date for the next formal review of this risk category definition, appetite thresholds, and associated controls. Ensures the taxonomy remains current with evolving regulatory requirements and firm risk profile.

attributes.name: notification_deadline_days
attributes.description: Maximum number of calendar days within which a risk incident under this category must be reported to the relevant regulatory authority (e.g., 72 hours / 3 days for GDPR personal data breaches under Article 33). Null if no mandatory external notification applies.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 33; SRA Reporting Obligations; PCI DSS Requirement 12.10

attributes.name: owner_role
attributes.description: Job title or role designation of the individual or function responsible for owning and managing risks under this category at the firm level (e.g., 'Chief Risk Officer', 'Data Protection Officer', 'General Counsel', 'Head of Compliance'). Distinct from matter-level risk owners.
attributes.references: ISO 31000:2018; GDPR Article 37 (DPO); SRA Code of Conduct

attributes.name: pii_relevance_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this risk category is directly associated with the handling, processing, or breach of Personally Identifiable Information (PII). When true, risk register entries under this category are subject to GDPR Article 33/34 breach notification obligations and DPA compliance controls.

attributes.name: professional_indemnity_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this risk category is relevant to the firm's professional indemnity insurance exposure. When true, incidents under this category must be reported to the firm's PI insurer and tracked in the claims management process.
attributes.references: SRA Indemnity Insurance Rules; ABA Model Rules Rule 1.1 (Competence); ISO 31000:2018

attributes.name: regulatory_framework
attributes.description: Primary regulatory or legal framework associated with this risk category (e.g., GDPR, ISO 27001, FATF AML, SOX, SRA Code of Conduct, ABA Model Rules, PCI DSS, CCPA). Used to link risk categories to applicable compliance obligations and regulatory reporting requirements.
attributes.references: GDPR; ISO/IEC 27001:2022; FATF; SOX; SRA; ABA; PCI DSS; CCPA

attributes.name: regulatory_reporting_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether incidents or risk register entries under this category must be reported to an external regulatory or supervisory body (e.g., ICO for GDPR breaches, SRA for serious misconduct, OFAC for sanctions violations). Triggers mandatory notification workflows.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 33; SRA Reporting Obligations; FATF; ABA Model Rules Rule 8.3

attributes.name: residual_risk_score
attributes.description: Numeric composite score representing the firm's residual (post-control) exposure for this risk category after mitigating controls have been applied. Used to assess whether the risk falls within the firm's risk appetite threshold.

attributes.name: review_frequency
attributes.description: Mandated frequency at which risk register entries under this category must be formally reviewed and updated by the responsible risk owner. Supports the firm's periodic risk assessment cycle and regulatory compliance obligations.
attributes.references: ISO 31000:2018; SRA Risk Outlook; ABA Model Rules

attributes.name: risk_appetite_level
attributes.description: Qualitative risk appetite classification for this category as declared in the firm's risk appetite framework. 'Zero tolerance' applies to categories such as sanctions breaches and money laundering; 'low' to professional indemnity and data privacy; 'moderate' to operational risk.
attributes.references: ISO 31000:2018; FATF Recommendations; SRA Code of Conduct

attributes.name: risk_appetite_threshold
attributes.description: Maximum acceptable residual risk score for this category as defined in the firm's risk appetite statement. Residual scores exceeding this threshold trigger escalation to the Risk Committee or Managing Partner. Aligns with SRA and ABA professional conduct obligations.
attributes.references: ISO 31000:2018; SRA Code of Conduct; ABA Model Rules of Professional Conduct

attributes.name: risk_domain
attributes.description: High-level domain grouping to which this risk category belongs, enabling portfolio-level risk aggregation and reporting. Maps to the firm's enterprise risk framework domains. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: professional|data_privacy|cybersecurity|sanctions_aml|reputational|operational|regulatory|financial|strategic — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ISO 31000:2018; FATF Recommendations; GDPR Article 32; ISO/IEC 27001:2022

attributes.name: risk_impact_rating
attributes.description: Standard impact rating assigned to this risk category, reflecting the potential severity of harm to the firm, its clients, or third parties if the risk materialises. Covers financial, reputational, regulatory, and operational impact dimensions.

attributes.name: risk_likelihood_rating
attributes.description: Standard likelihood rating assigned to this risk category within the firm's risk appetite framework, indicating the probability of occurrence. Used as the default likelihood baseline when creating new risk register entries under this category.
attributes.references: ISO 31000:2018; SRA Risk Outlook; ABA Model Rules

attributes.name: risk_type
attributes.description: Classification of the risk category by its nature within the risk management lifecycle: inherent (pre-control), residual (post-control), emerging (newly identified), or systemic (firm-wide structural exposure). Drives how risk assessments are scoped and reported.

attributes.name: sort_order
attributes.description: Integer value controlling the display sequence of this risk category in risk registers, dashboards, and dropdown selection lists. Lower values appear first. Enables consistent presentation across risk management tools and reports.

attributes.name: utbms_task_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: Uniform Task-Based Management System (UTBMS) Task Code
attributes.description: UTBMS task code associated with the legal work type most commonly linked to this risk category (e.g., L430 for Written Discovery in litigation risk, C300 for Due Diligence in transactional risk). Enables cross-referencing between risk categories and billing/matter management data in Elite 3E.
attributes.references: LEDES/UTBMS Code Set; ABA TECHSHOW; Elite 3E Practice Management

products.name: assessment
products.description: Formal risk assessment record capturing the structured evaluation of a specific risk item at a point in time. Records inherent risk score, control effectiveness rating, residual risk score, likelihood rating, impact rating, risk appetite threshold comparison, assessor identity, assessment methodology (qualitative/quantitative), and next review date. Supports periodic risk review cycles mandated by ISO 27001 and SRA requirements.

attributes.name: assessment_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each formal risk assessment record within the enterprise risk register. Primary key for the risk_assessment data product.
attributes.references: ISO 27001:2022 Clause 6.1.2; SRA Code of Conduct 2019

attributes.name: appetite_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to risk.risk_appetite. Business justification: Risk assessments compare residual risk against defined appetite thresholds. risk_assessment has risk_appetite_threshold (DECIMAL) which should be replaced by FK to the authoritative risk_appetite tabl

attributes.name: assessment_treatment_owner_attorney_profile_id
attributes.description: Reference to the timekeeper or workforce member accountable for implementing the risk treatment actions. Distinct from the assessor; supports accountability and escalation workflows.
attributes.references: ISO 27001:2022 Clause 6.1.3; SRA Code of Conduct 2019

attributes.name: category_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to risk.risk_category. Business justification: risk_assessment has risk_category (STRING) attribute that should normalize to the risk_category reference table. This is the authoritative taxonomy for risk categories. Standard reference FK pattern.

attributes.name: matter_id
attributes.description: Reference to the legal matter associated with this risk assessment, where the assessment is matter-specific (e.g., litigation exposure, transaction risk). Null for firm-level enterprise risk assessments.
attributes.references: SRA Code of Conduct 2019; Elite 3E Matter Management

attributes.name: profile_id
attributes.description: Reference to the client whose engagement or matter is the subject of this risk assessment. Supports client-level risk aggregation and Know Your Client (KYC) / Anti-Money Laundering (AML) compliance reporting.
attributes.references: FATF Recommendation 10; SRA AML Guidance 2023; GDPR Article 5

attributes.name: register_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent risk item in the enterprise risk register that this assessment evaluates. Links the point-in-time assessment to the persistent risk record.
attributes.references: ISO 27001:2022 Clause 6.1.2; SRA Code of Conduct 2019

attributes.name: reviewer_attorney_profile_id
attributes.description: Reference to the senior timekeeper or partner who reviewed and approved this risk assessment. Distinct from the assessor; supports segregation of duties and sign-off audit trail.
attributes.references: ISO 27001:2022 Clause 9.3; SRA Standards and Regulations 2019

attributes.name: risk_control_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to risk.risk_control. Business justification: Risk assessments evaluate the effectiveness of specific controls. Business semantics: 'this assessment evaluated this control.' Valid relationship for control effectiveness tracking.

attributes.name: assessment_date
attributes.description: The calendar date on which the formal risk assessment was conducted. Represents the principal business event date for this assessment cycle, distinct from record creation timestamp.
attributes.references: ISO 27001:2022 Clause 6.1.2; SRA Standards and Regulations 2019

attributes.name: assessment_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the risk assessment record. Draft indicates work in progress; in_review indicates pending senior sign-off; approved indicates formally accepted; superseded indicates replaced by a newer assessment; closed indicates the risk has been retired.
attributes.references: ISO 27001:2022 Clause 6.1.2; SRA Code of Conduct 2019

attributes.name: control_effectiveness_rating
attributes.description: Assessment of how well the existing controls mitigate the identified risk. Drives the reduction from inherent to residual risk score. Evaluated against the firm's control framework aligned with ISO 27001 Annex A controls.
attributes.references: ISO 27001:2022 Annex A; SRA Code of Conduct 2019

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this risk assessment record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail and data lineage requirements under ISO 27001 and GDPR.

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the estimated financial exposure amount (e.g., GBP, USD, EUR). Supports multi-currency risk reporting for international matters.

attributes.name: escalation_level
attributes.description: The organisational level to which this risk has been escalated based on its residual risk score relative to appetite. None indicates no escalation required; practice_group to practice group risk lead; risk_committee to the firm's Risk and Compliance Committee; board to the Managing Partner or Board.
attributes.references: SRA Code of Conduct 2019; ISO 27001:2022 Clause 9.3; IBA Guidelines on Conflicts of Interest

attributes.name: estimated_financial_exposure
attributes.description: Estimated maximum financial exposure or loss amount associated with this risk, expressed in the firm's base currency. Used for professional indemnity reserve calculations and risk-weighted financial reporting. Classified confidential as it contains sensitive financial strategy data.
attributes.references: SRA Indemnity Insurance Rules; ISO 31000:2018 Clause 6.4.3; SOX Section 404

attributes.name: inherent_impact_rating
attributes.description: Qualitative rating of the severity of consequence if the risk event occurs before any controls are applied. Considers financial, reputational, regulatory, and operational dimensions of impact.

attributes.name: inherent_likelihood_rating
attributes.description: Qualitative rating of the probability that the risk event will occur before any controls are applied. Represents the raw, unmitigated likelihood on a five-point scale aligned with the firm's risk appetite framework.

attributes.name: inherent_risk_score
attributes.description: Numerical composite score representing the unmitigated risk level, typically derived as the product of inherent likelihood and inherent impact ratings mapped to a numeric scale. Used for risk prioritisation before control assessment.

attributes.name: is_dpia_required
attributes.business_glossary_term: Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA) Required Indicator
attributes.description: Indicates whether a Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA) is required for this risk item under GDPR Article 35. True when the risk involves high-risk processing of personal data, triggering mandatory DPIA before processing commences.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 35; ICO DPIA Guidance; DPA 2018

attributes.name: is_lpp_sensitive
attributes.description: Indicates whether this risk assessment record or its associated matter is subject to Legal Professional Privilege (LPP). When True, access is restricted to authorised legal personnel and the record is excluded from certain regulatory disclosures.
attributes.references: LPP common law principles; SRA Code of Conduct 2019; Three Rivers District Council v Bank of England [2004]

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this risk assessment record was most recently modified. Used for change tracking, optimistic concurrency control, and audit compliance.

attributes.name: methodology
attributes.description: Methodology used to evaluate the risk. Qualitative uses descriptive scales; quantitative uses numerical probability and financial impact modelling; semi_quantitative combines both approaches. Determines how inherent and residual scores are interpreted.

attributes.name: next_review_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date by which this risk assessment must be reviewed and refreshed. Drives the periodic risk review cycle mandated by ISO 27001 and SRA requirements. Alerts are triggered when this date approaches.
attributes.references: ISO 27001:2022 Clause 8.2; SRA Code of Conduct 2019 Rule 2.1

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for the assessor to record additional context, caveats, assumptions, or observations that do not fit structured fields. Classified confidential as notes may contain sensitive matter or client strategy information.
attributes.references: SRA Code of Conduct 2019; ISO 27001:2022 Clause 6.1.2

attributes.name: pii_data_involved
attributes.business_glossary_term: Personally Identifiable Information (PII) Data Involved Indicator
attributes.description: Indicates whether the risk scenario involves Personally Identifiable Information (PII) or personal data as defined under GDPR. True triggers additional data protection controls and potential DPIA requirement.

attributes.name: reference
attributes.description: Externally-known business identifier for the risk assessment, formatted as RA-{YYYY}-{NNNNNN}. Used in correspondence, audit trails, and regulatory submissions to uniquely reference a specific assessment cycle.
attributes.references: ISO 27001:2022 Clause 6.1.2; SRA Standards and Regulations 2019

attributes.name: regulatory_framework
attributes.description: The primary regulatory or compliance framework under which this risk assessment is conducted (e.g., ISO 27001, GDPR, SRA, FATF, SOX, PCI DSS, CCPA). Supports regulatory reporting segmentation and framework-specific risk aggregation.
attributes.references: ISO 27001:2022; GDPR Article 35; FATF Recommendations; SRA Standards 2019; SOX Section 404

attributes.name: residual_impact_rating
attributes.description: Qualitative rating of the severity of consequence after existing controls have been applied. Used alongside residual likelihood to compute the residual risk score.

attributes.name: residual_likelihood_rating
attributes.description: Qualitative rating of the probability that the risk event will occur after existing controls have been applied. Reflects the post-control likelihood used to determine whether residual risk is within appetite.

attributes.name: residual_risk_score
attributes.description: Numerical composite score representing the remaining risk level after controls are applied. Compared against the risk appetite threshold to determine whether the risk is acceptable or requires further treatment.
attributes.references: ISO 27001:2022 Clause 6.1.3; SRA Standards and Regulations 2019

attributes.name: review_cycle
attributes.description: The mandated frequency at which this risk assessment must be reviewed and refreshed. Drives scheduling of next_review_date and supports compliance with ISO 27001 periodic review requirements.
attributes.references: ISO 27001:2022 Clause 8.2; SRA Code of Conduct 2019

attributes.name: risk_description
attributes.description: Detailed narrative description of the risk scenario, including the threat source, vulnerability, and potential consequence. May contain sensitive matter or client information and is classified confidential. Supports Legal Professional Privilege (LPP) considerations.
attributes.references: ISO 27001:2022 Clause 6.1.2; SRA Code of Conduct 2019; LPP principles

attributes.name: risk_domain
attributes.description: High-level classification of the risk domain being assessed. Professional indemnity covers malpractice exposure; data_breach covers PII/GDPR incidents; cybersecurity covers ISO 27001 threats; sanctions covers FATF/AML screening; reputational covers client or matter reputational flags. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: professional_indemnity|data_breach|cybersecurity|sanctions|reputational|operational|regulatory|financial — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ISO 27001:2022 Clause 6.1.2; FATF Recommendations; SRA Code of Conduct 2019

attributes.name: risk_score_scale
attributes.description: The numerical scale used for inherent and residual risk scoring in this assessment (e.g., 1_to_5, 1_to_10, 1_to_25). Ensures correct interpretation of scores when the firm operates multiple scoring frameworks across practice groups.

attributes.name: risk_title
attributes.description: Short, human-readable label for the risk item being assessed (e.g., 'Unauthorised disclosure of privileged documents', 'Sanctions exposure — client XYZ'). Used in dashboards, reports, and risk register summaries.
attributes.references: ISO 27001:2022 Clause 6.1.2; SRA Standards and Regulations 2019

attributes.name: risk_treatment_option
attributes.description: The selected risk treatment strategy for this assessment. Accept means the firm tolerates the residual risk; mitigate means additional controls will be implemented; transfer means risk is shifted (e.g., via professional indemnity insurance); avoid means the risk-generating activity is discontinued.

attributes.name: sanctions_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this risk assessment was triggered by or relates to a sanctions screening alert (e.g., OFAC, UN, EU sanctions lists). True requires escalation to the firm's Anti-Money Laundering (AML) compliance officer.
attributes.references: FATF Recommendation 10; SRA AML Guidance 2023; OFAC SDN List

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Name of the operational system of record from which this risk assessment originated or was ingested (e.g., Intapp Conflicts, Elite 3E, manual entry). Supports data lineage tracking in the Databricks Silver Layer.

attributes.name: treatment_description
attributes.description: Narrative description of the specific actions, controls, or measures to be implemented under the selected risk treatment option. Classified confidential as it may contain sensitive operational or legal strategy information.
attributes.references: ISO 27001:2022 Clause 6.1.3; SRA Code of Conduct 2019

attributes.name: treatment_due_date
attributes.description: Target date by which the agreed risk treatment actions must be completed. Used for tracking remediation progress and escalation when treatment is overdue.
attributes.references: ISO 27001:2022 Clause 6.1.3; SRA Standards and Regulations 2019

attributes.name: within_appetite
attributes.description: Indicates whether the residual risk score falls within the firm's defined risk appetite threshold. True means the risk is acceptable; False triggers mandatory escalation and treatment action. Derived from comparing residual_risk_score against risk_appetite_threshold but stored for reporting efficiency.
attributes.references: ISO 27001:2022 Clause 6.1.3; SRA Standards and Regulations 2019

attributes.name: assessment_attorney_profile_id
attributes.description: Reference to the timekeeper or workforce member who conducted and is responsible for this risk assessment. Supports accountability tracking and assessor workload reporting.
attributes.references: ISO 27001:2022 Clause 6.1.2; SRA Code of Conduct 2019

products.name: risk_control
products.description: Catalog of risk controls and mitigating measures implemented to address identified risks, including complete control testing and audit history. Each record captures control type (preventive, detective, corrective), control owner, implementation status, operational effectiveness rating, and linkage to mitigated risk items. Embeds the full testing lifecycle: each test instance records test date, tester identity, test methodology, evidence reference, pass/fail outcome, deficiencies identified, remediation required flag, and remediation due date. Provides the consolidated control-and-test audit trail required for ISO 27001 certification and SRA compliance reviews. Aligned to ISO 27001 Annex A control framework.

attributes.name: risk_control_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each risk control record in the enterprise risk register. Primary key for the risk_control data product.
attributes.references: ISO 27001:2022 Annex A; SRA Standards and Regulations

attributes.name: category_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to risk.risk_category. Business justification: Controls are designed to mitigate specific categories of risk. risk_control has control_category (STRING) which should normalize to risk_category table for taxonomy consistency.

attributes.name: register_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent risk item in the enterprise risk register that this control is designed to mitigate. Links the control to its associated risk exposure.
attributes.references: ISO 27001:2022 Clause 6.1.3; SRA Code of Conduct

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: Date on which this control was formally approved by the designated approver. Required for ISO 27001 governance documentation and SRA compliance audit trails.

attributes.name: automation_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the control is automated (True) or manual (False). Automated controls are executed by systems (e.g., Intapp Conflicts automated screening, iManage access controls); manual controls rely on human action. Informs risk appetite assessments and operational resilience planning.
attributes.references: ISO 27001:2022 Annex A; SRA Code of Conduct

attributes.name: control_description
attributes.description: Detailed narrative describing the purpose, scope, and mechanism of the control, including how it addresses the identified risk. Supports ISO 27001 Statement of Applicability (SoA) documentation.
attributes.references: ISO 27001:2022 Clause 6.1.3; SRA Standards and Regulations

attributes.name: control_name
attributes.description: Short, human-readable title of the risk control (e.g., 'Privileged Access Review', 'PII Data Encryption at Rest', 'Conflict Check Gate'). Used in dashboards, audit reports, and SRA compliance reviews.
attributes.references: ISO 27001:2022 Annex A; ABA Model Rules of Professional Conduct

attributes.name: control_type
attributes.description: Classification of the control by its functional purpose in the risk management lifecycle. Preventive controls stop risk events; detective controls identify them; corrective controls remediate them; deterrent controls discourage threats; compensating controls substitute for primary controls; directive controls mandate behaviour.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time at which this risk control record was first created in the enterprise risk register. Provides the audit trail start point for ISO 27001 and SRA compliance reviews.

attributes.name: deficiency_description
attributes.description: Narrative description of any control deficiency, gap, or weakness identified during the most recent test. Null if no deficiency was found. Feeds the remediation workflow and is referenced in ISO 27001 nonconformity reports and SRA compliance submissions.
attributes.references: ISO 27001:2022 Clause 10.1; SRA Standards and Regulations

attributes.name: design_effectiveness_rating
attributes.description: Assessment of whether the control is suitably designed to address the risk it targets, independent of whether it is operating correctly. Adequate: design is fit for purpose. Inadequate: design has structural gaps. Not Assessed: design review not yet completed.

attributes.name: domain
attributes.description: Business risk domain that this control primarily addresses (e.g., 'Professional Indemnity', 'Data Privacy / GDPR', 'Cybersecurity', 'Sanctions Screening', 'Reputational Risk', 'Anti-Money Laundering (AML)', 'Conflict of Interest'). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: professional_indemnity|data_privacy|cybersecurity|sanctions_screening|reputational|aml|conflict_of_interest|regulatory_compliance — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: SRA Code of Conduct; FATF Recommendations; GDPR Article 32; ISO 27001:2022

attributes.name: evidence_reference
attributes.description: Document Management System (DMS) reference or iManage Work document identifier for the evidence artefact supporting the most recent control test (e.g., screenshots, logs, policy documents, access reports). Required for ISO 27001 audit evidence packages.
attributes.references: ISO 27001:2022 Clause 9.1; iManage Work DMS; SRA Compliance Framework

attributes.name: gdpr_relevant_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) Relevant Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this control is relevant to the firm's General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) compliance obligations, including Personally Identifiable Information (PII) protection and data breach prevention (True) or not (False). Supports Data Protection Officer (DPO) reporting.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 32; ICO Accountability Framework; DPA 2018

attributes.name: implementation_date
attributes.description: The date on which the control was fully implemented and became operational. Used to calculate control age, schedule periodic reviews, and demonstrate timely remediation to SRA and ISO 27001 auditors.

attributes.name: implementation_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the control's implementation. Planned: approved but not yet started. In Progress: actively being deployed. Implemented: fully operational. Deferred: postponed with documented rationale. Not Applicable: formally excluded from scope with SoA justification.

attributes.name: inherent_risk_rating
attributes.description: The assessed level of risk exposure before any controls are applied. Provides the baseline against which control effectiveness is measured. Required for ISO 27001 risk treatment plan documentation.

attributes.name: iso_annex_a_reference
attributes.description: The specific ISO 27001:2022 Annex A control identifier to which this control maps (e.g., A.5.1, A.8.24). Enables traceability between the firm's control catalogue and the ISO certification framework. Required for Statement of Applicability (SoA) reporting.

attributes.name: iso_soa_included_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: ISO 27001 Statement of Applicability (SoA) Included Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this control is included in the firm's ISO 27001 Statement of Applicability (SoA) (True) or formally excluded with documented justification (False). Mandatory field for ISO 27001 certification maintenance.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time at which this risk control record was most recently updated. Supports change tracking, audit trail requirements, and incremental data loading in the Databricks Silver Layer.

attributes.name: last_test_date
attributes.description: Date on which the most recently completed control test instance was executed. Used to determine whether the control is within its required testing cadence and to flag overdue tests for the compliance team.
attributes.references: ISO 27001:2022 Clause 9.1; SRA Annual Compliance Declaration

attributes.name: last_test_outcome
attributes.description: Result of the most recently completed control test instance. Pass: control operated as designed. Fail: control did not operate as designed. Partial Pass: control operated with minor deficiencies. Not Applicable: test was not applicable in the period.

attributes.name: lpp_scope_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this control is specifically designed to protect Legal Professional Privilege (LPP) material from unauthorised disclosure (True) or not (False). Critical for controls governing iManage Work access, Relativity matter workspaces, and client communication channels.
attributes.references: ABA Model Rules of Professional Conduct Rule 1.6; SRA Code of Conduct; Law Society of England and Wales Practice Notes

attributes.name: mitigates_risk
attributes.description: FK to risk.risk_register.risk_register_id — Controls are implemented to mitigate specific risks. This many-to-many relationship (via junction or FK array) is essential for control-to-risk traceability required by ISO 27001.

attributes.name: next_review_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date for the next periodic review or re-assessment of the control's design and operational effectiveness. Drives the control testing calendar and ensures compliance with ISO 27001 continuous improvement requirements.
attributes.references: ISO 27001:2022 Clause 9.1; SRA Annual Compliance Declaration

attributes.name: operational_effectiveness_rating
attributes.description: Assessment of how well the control is operating in practice to mitigate the associated risk. Derived from the most recent completed test cycle. Effective: control operates as designed. Partially Effective: control operates but with gaps. Ineffective: control fails to mitigate risk. Not Tested: no test has been completed.
attributes.references: ISO 27001:2022 Clause 9.1; SRA Standards and Regulations

attributes.name: pii_scope_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this control specifically addresses the protection of Personally Identifiable Information (PII) held by the firm (True) or not (False). Used to scope GDPR Article 32 technical and organisational measures documentation.

attributes.name: priority
attributes.description: Business-assigned priority level for this control, reflecting the criticality of the risk it mitigates and the urgency of maintaining its effectiveness. Used to prioritise control testing resources and remediation efforts.

attributes.name: reference_code
attributes.description: Externally-known unique alphanumeric code assigned to this control, aligned to the ISO 27001 Annex A control numbering scheme or the firm's internal control catalogue (e.g., ISO-A.8.1-001). Used for cross-referencing in audit reports and SRA compliance submissions.
attributes.references: ISO 27001:2022 Annex A; SRA Compliance Framework

attributes.name: remediation_completed_date
attributes.description: Date on which the remediation action was confirmed as completed and verified. Null if remediation is not yet complete. Used to close the deficiency lifecycle and update the ISO 27001 nonconformity register.

attributes.name: remediation_due_date
attributes.description: Target date by which the identified control deficiency must be remediated. Null if no remediation is required. Used to track overdue remediations and escalate to the Risk Committee and SRA as required.
attributes.references: ISO 27001:2022 Clause 10.1; SRA Standards and Regulations

attributes.name: remediation_required_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a remediation action is required as a result of the most recent control test (True) or not (False). Triggers the remediation workflow and escalation process for overdue items.

attributes.name: remediation_status
attributes.description: Current status of the remediation action for any identified control deficiency. Not Required: no deficiency found. Open: remediation identified but not started. In Progress: remediation underway. Completed: deficiency resolved and verified. Overdue: remediation due date has passed without completion.

attributes.name: residual_risk_rating
attributes.description: The assessed level of risk remaining after this control and any other mitigating measures are applied. Represents the firm's net exposure. Used in risk appetite reporting to the firm's Risk Committee and in SRA regulatory submissions.
attributes.references: ISO 27001:2022 Clause 6.1.2; SRA Standards and Regulations; ABA Model Rules

attributes.name: review_frequency
attributes.description: Mandated frequency at which this control must be reviewed and tested. Determines the cadence of scheduled test instances and supports audit planning for ISO 27001 surveillance audits and SRA compliance reviews.
attributes.references: ISO 27001:2022 Clause 9.1; SRA Standards and Regulations

attributes.name: soa_exclusion_justification
attributes.description: Documented rationale for excluding this control from the ISO 27001 Statement of Applicability (SoA). Null if the control is included. Required by ISO 27001:2022 Clause 6.1.3(d) for all excluded Annex A controls.

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Name of the operational system of record in which this control is primarily configured or enforced (e.g., 'Intapp Conflicts', 'iManage Work', 'Relativity', 'SAP SuccessFactors'). Supports lineage tracing and system-level risk assessments.

attributes.name: sra_reportable_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a control failure or deficiency associated with this control is reportable to the Solicitors Regulation Authority (SRA) under mandatory reporting obligations (True) or not (False). Supports regulatory breach management workflows.
attributes.references: SRA Standards and Regulations; SRA Code of Conduct 2019

attributes.name: test_methodology
attributes.description: The approach used to test the control in the most recent test instance. Inquiry: interviews with control operators. Observation: direct observation of control execution. Inspection: review of evidence documents. Re-performance: independent re-execution of the control. Walkthrough: end-to-end process trace. Automated Scan: system-generated test.
attributes.references: ISO 27001:2022 Clause 9.1; ISAE 3402; SRA Compliance Framework

attributes.name: to_register
attributes.description: FK to risk.risk_register.risk_register_id — Controls mitigate specific risks. The risk_control description states 'linkage to mitigated risk items'. This FK is essential for control-to-risk traceability required by ISO 27001.

attributes.name: to_risk_register
attributes.description: FK to risk.risk_register.risk_register_id — Controls mitigate specific risks. The many-to-many relationship between controls and risk items is the core of risk management. Without this link, you cannot answer 'what controls address this risk?'

attributes.name: primary_risk_attorney_profile_id
attributes.description: Reference to the timekeeper or workforce member who is accountable for the design, implementation, and ongoing effectiveness of this control.
attributes.references: ISO 27001:2022 Clause 5.3; SRA Standards and Regulations

attributes.name: tertiary_risk_remediation_owner_attorney_profile_id
attributes.description: Reference to the timekeeper or workforce member accountable for completing the remediation action. Null if no remediation is required. Supports escalation workflows and accountability tracking.
attributes.references: ISO 27001:2022 Clause 10.1; SRA Standards and Regulations

attributes.name: quaternary_risk_approved_by_attorney_profile_id
attributes.description: Reference to the timekeeper or senior risk officer who formally approved this control for inclusion in the risk register and Statement of Applicability. Supports governance and segregation of duties requirements.
attributes.references: ISO 27001:2022 Clause 5.3; SRA Standards and Regulations

products.name: indemnity_exposure
products.description: Professional indemnity (PI) exposure record tracking the firm's estimated liability exposure on a per-matter or per-claim basis. Captures exposure type (negligence, breach of duty, conflict of interest), estimated claim value, reserve amount, insurer notified flag, notification date, policy year, excess amount, and current exposure status. Feeds the firm's PI insurance renewal process and risk appetite monitoring.

attributes.name: indemnity_exposure_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each professional indemnity exposure record. Primary key for the indemnity_exposure data product within the risk domain.
attributes.references: Elite 3E Practice Management and Financial System

attributes.name: category_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to risk.risk_category. Business justification: Indemnity exposures are categorized by risk type. indemnity_exposure has exposure_type (STRING) which should normalize to risk_category for taxonomy consistency.

attributes.name: check_id
attributes.description: Reference to the conflict check record that identified or is associated with the conflict-of-interest dimension of this exposure. Links to the conflict domain to provide the full conflict screening context without duplicating conflict data.
attributes.references: Intapp Conflicts New Business Intake; ABA Model Rules of Professional Conduct Rules 1.7-1.10; SRA Code of Conduct

attributes.name: escalation_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to risk.risk_escalation. Business justification: High-value indemnity exposures may trigger escalations to governance bodies. Valid business relationship for PI risk management.

attributes.name: invoice_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to billing.invoice. Business justification: Professional indemnity exposures often arise from billing disputes or fee-related client complaints. Firms link PI exposure to the triggering invoice for reserve calculation, insurer notification, and

attributes.name: matter_id
attributes.description: Reference to the legal matter or case from which this professional indemnity exposure arises. Links the exposure record to the matter management domain for context on the underlying work.

attributes.name: pi_claim_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to risk.pi_claim. Business justification: An indemnity exposure can crystallize into a formal PI claim. The exposure is the 'potential liability' stage; the claim is the 'formal claim filed' stage. Valid progression relationship. Replaces cla

attributes.name: profile_id
attributes.description: Reference to the client entity associated with this indemnity exposure. Enables risk aggregation by client and supports Know Your Client (KYC) and conflict-check linkage.
attributes.references: Elite 3E Client/Matter Management; Intapp Conflicts New Business Intake

attributes.name: register_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to risk.risk_register. Business justification: Professional indemnity exposures are enterprise risks and should be tracked in the risk register. Valid business relationship for PI risk aggregation.

attributes.name: responsible_timekeeper_id
attributes.description: Reference to the timekeeper (partner, associate, or fee-earner) identified as the responsible professional for the matter giving rise to this exposure. Used for accountability tracking and PI insurance reporting.
attributes.references: Aderant Expert Timekeeper Management; SRA Indemnity Insurance Rules

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp at which this indemnity exposure record was first created in the risk register. Provides the audit trail anchor for the record's lifecycle and supports data lineage tracking in the Databricks Silver Layer.
attributes.references: ISO 27001 Information Security Management; GDPR Article 5 (Integrity and Confidentiality); General Data Protection Regulation

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for all monetary amounts on this exposure record (estimated_claim_value, reserve_amount, excess_amount, settlement_amount). Supports multi-currency PI exposure reporting for international practices.
attributes.references: ISO 4217 Currency Codes; IFRS 17 Insurance Contracts

attributes.name: estimated_claim_value
attributes.description: The firm's current best estimate of the total monetary value of the potential claim arising from this exposure, expressed in the firm's base currency. Used for reserve-setting, PI insurance renewal, and risk appetite monitoring. Reviewed and updated as new information becomes available.
attributes.references: SRA Indemnity Insurance Rules; IFRS 17 Insurance Contracts; ABA Risk Management Guidelines

attributes.name: excess_amount
attributes.description: The amount of the policy excess (deductible) applicable to this exposure under the firm's professional indemnity insurance policy. Represents the portion of any claim the firm must bear before insurer coverage is triggered. Critical for net exposure calculation.
attributes.references: SRA Indemnity Insurance Rules; Insurance Act 2015 (UK); ABA Standing Committee on Lawyers' Professional Liability

attributes.name: exposure_linked_to_risk
attributes.description: FK to risk.risk_register.risk_register_id — PI exposures should reference the risk register item they relate to for consolidated risk reporting.

attributes.name: exposure_narrative
attributes.description: Free-text description of the circumstances giving rise to this professional indemnity exposure, including the nature of the alleged failing, the client's complaint, and any relevant background. Confidential and subject to Legal Professional Privilege (LPP) where applicable.
attributes.references: ABA Risk Management Guidelines; SRA Code of Conduct; Legal Professional Privilege (LPP) doctrine

attributes.name: exposure_reference
attributes.description: Externally-known business reference number assigned to this PI exposure record, used in correspondence with insurers, brokers, and internal risk committees. Format: PI-{YYYY}-{NNNNNN}.
attributes.references: American Bar Association (ABA) Risk Management Guidelines; Solicitors Regulation Authority (SRA) Indemnity Insurance Rules

attributes.name: exposure_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the indemnity exposure record, from initial identification through insurer notification, active reservation, litigation, and final closure. Drives workflow routing and risk appetite monitoring.
attributes.references: SRA Indemnity Insurance Rules; ABA Risk Management Guidelines; ISO 31000 Risk Management

attributes.name: external_counsel_engaged_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the firm has engaged external legal counsel to advise on or defend the claim arising from this exposure. True if external counsel has been instructed; False if the matter is being handled internally or no claim has been made.
attributes.references: ABA Model Rules of Professional Conduct; SRA Code of Conduct; Law Society of England and Wales

attributes.name: external_counsel_firm
attributes.description: Name of the external law firm engaged to advise on or defend the claim arising from this exposure. Populated when external_counsel_engaged_flag is True. Used for conflict screening and cost tracking.
attributes.references: ABA Model Rules of Professional Conduct; SRA Code of Conduct

attributes.name: identified_date
attributes.description: The date on which the firm first became aware of the potential professional indemnity exposure. Critical for determining the policy year applicable and meeting insurer notification deadlines.
attributes.references: SRA Indemnity Insurance Rules; ABA Model Rules of Professional Conduct Rule 1.4

attributes.name: insurer_name
attributes.description: Name of the professional indemnity insurer or lead underwriter carrying the risk for this exposure. Confidential commercial information used for insurer relationship management and claims coordination.
attributes.references: SRA Indemnity Insurance Rules; ABA Standing Committee on Lawyers' Professional Liability

attributes.name: insurer_notification_date
attributes.description: The date on which the firm formally notified its professional indemnity insurer of this exposure. Null if insurer_notified_flag is False. Used to verify compliance with policy notification obligations and to anchor the claims-made trigger.
attributes.references: SRA Indemnity Insurance Rules; Insurance Act 2015 (UK); ABA Standing Committee on Lawyers' Professional Liability

attributes.name: insurer_notified_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the firm's professional indemnity insurer has been formally notified of this exposure. A value of True confirms notification has been made; False indicates notification is pending or not yet required.
attributes.references: SRA Indemnity Insurance Rules; ABA Standing Committee on Lawyers' Professional Liability

attributes.name: internal_investigation_status
attributes.description: Current status of the firm's internal investigation into the circumstances giving rise to this exposure. Tracks whether a root cause analysis has been initiated, is ongoing, or has been completed and findings documented.
attributes.references: ABA Risk Management Guidelines; ISO 31000 Risk Management; Law Society of England and Wales Risk Management Guidance

attributes.name: investigation_completed_date
attributes.description: The date on which the firm's internal investigation into this exposure was formally concluded and findings documented. Null if internal_investigation_status is not 'completed'. Used for risk governance reporting.
attributes.references: ABA Risk Management Guidelines; ISO 31000 Risk Management

attributes.name: jurisdiction
attributes.description: The legal jurisdiction (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 or alpha-3 country code) in which the matter giving rise to this exposure was conducted and where any claim would be adjudicated. Determines applicable professional conduct rules and limitation periods.
attributes.references: ISO 3166-1; ABA Model Rules of Professional Conduct; Law Society of England and Wales; International Bar Association (IBA) Guidelines

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp at which this indemnity exposure record was most recently modified. Used for incremental data pipeline processing, change detection, and audit trail maintenance in the Databricks Silver Layer.
attributes.references: ISO 27001 Information Security Management; GDPR Article 5 (Integrity and Confidentiality); General Data Protection Regulation

attributes.name: limitation_expiry_date
attributes.description: The date on which the applicable statute of limitations or limitation period for a claim arising from this exposure expires. Critical for risk management and determining whether an exposure can still give rise to a formal claim. Varies by jurisdiction and exposure type.
attributes.references: Limitation Act 1980 (UK); ABA Model Rules of Professional Conduct; jurisdiction-specific limitation statutes

attributes.name: lpp_applies_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether Legal Professional Privilege (LPP) applies to the documents and communications associated with this exposure record, restricting disclosure in any subsequent litigation or regulatory investigation. True if LPP is asserted; False if not applicable or waived.
attributes.references: Legal Professional Privilege (LPP) doctrine; Three Rivers District Council v Bank of England [2004] UKHL 48; ABA Model Rules of Professional Conduct Rule 1.6

attributes.name: matter_close_date
attributes.description: The date on which the underlying legal matter from which this exposure arises was formally closed in the practice management system. Used to calculate the elapsed time between matter closure and exposure identification, informing limitation period analysis.
attributes.references: Elite 3E Matter Management Module; SRA Indemnity Insurance Rules

attributes.name: pi_renewal_submission_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this exposure record has been included in the firm's most recent professional indemnity insurance renewal submission to the insurer or broker. True confirms inclusion; False indicates it is pending inclusion or not yet due.
attributes.references: SRA Indemnity Insurance Rules; ABA Standing Committee on Lawyers' Professional Liability

attributes.name: policy_number
attributes.description: The unique policy number of the professional indemnity insurance policy under which this exposure is covered. Confidential commercial information used to reference the specific insurer contract during claims handling.
attributes.references: SRA Indemnity Insurance Rules; Insurance Act 2015 (UK)

attributes.name: policy_year
attributes.description: The insurance policy year (e.g., 2024-2025) under which this exposure is to be reported and reserved. Determines which insurer and policy limits apply. Format: YYYY-YYYY representing the policy inception and expiry years.
attributes.references: SRA Indemnity Insurance Rules; ABA Standing Committee on Lawyers' Professional Liability; Insurance Act 2015 (UK)

attributes.name: practice_area
attributes.description: The legal practice area (e.g., Corporate, Litigation, Real Estate, Employment, Intellectual Property) associated with the matter giving rise to this exposure. Enables risk concentration analysis by practice group and informs PI insurance underwriting submissions. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: corporate|litigation|real_estate|employment|intellectual_property|regulatory_compliance|tax|private_client|other — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: American Bar Association (ABA) Practice Area Classifications; Law Society of England and Wales Practice Divisions

attributes.name: regulatory_body
attributes.description: Name of the regulatory body to which this exposure has been or may be referred (e.g., Solicitors Regulation Authority, State Bar Association, Legal Services Board). Populated when regulatory_referral_flag is True.
attributes.references: SRA Code of Conduct; ABA Model Rules of Professional Conduct; Legal Services Board

attributes.name: regulatory_referral_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this exposure has been or is required to be referred to a regulatory body (e.g., SRA, State Bar Association, Legal Services Board). True if a regulatory referral has been made or is pending. Drives compliance domain notifications.
attributes.references: SRA Code of Conduct; ABA Model Rules of Professional Conduct Rule 8.3; Legal Services Board Regulatory Framework

attributes.name: reputational_risk_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this exposure carries a significant reputational risk dimension beyond the financial liability, such as media attention, regulatory scrutiny, or high-profile client involvement. True triggers enhanced monitoring and senior partner escalation.
attributes.references: ABA Risk Management Guidelines; Law Society of England and Wales Risk Management Guidance; ISO 31000 Risk Management

attributes.name: reserve_amount
attributes.description: The financial reserve set aside by the firm (or agreed with the insurer) to cover the estimated liability for this exposure. Feeds the firm's balance sheet provisioning and PI insurance renewal submissions. Distinct from the estimated claim value as it reflects the agreed reserving position.
attributes.references: SRA Indemnity Insurance Rules; IFRS 17 Insurance Contracts; International Accounting Standards (IAS) 37 Provisions

attributes.name: reserve_last_reviewed_date
attributes.description: The date on which the financial reserve for this exposure was most recently reviewed and confirmed or updated by the risk committee or responsible partner. Ensures reserves remain current and supports PI insurance renewal accuracy.
attributes.references: SRA Indemnity Insurance Rules; IFRS 17 Insurance Contracts; IAS 37 Provisions

attributes.name: risk_severity
attributes.description: The firm's internal risk severity rating for this exposure, reflecting the combination of estimated financial impact and likelihood of a formal claim being made. Drives escalation protocols, partner notification requirements, and risk committee reporting.
attributes.references: ISO 31000 Risk Management; ABA Risk Management Guidelines; SRA Risk Outlook

attributes.name: root_cause_category
attributes.description: High-level categorisation of the root cause of the professional failing giving rise to this exposure, as determined during the firm's internal investigation. Used for risk management trend analysis and process improvement initiatives.
attributes.references: ISO 31000 Risk Management; ABA Risk Management Guidelines; Law Society of England and Wales Risk Management Guidance

attributes.name: settlement_amount
attributes.description: The actual monetary amount agreed in settlement of the claim arising from this exposure. Populated only when exposure_status is 'closed' and the matter was resolved by settlement. Null for open or litigated exposures. Used for actuarial analysis and PI renewal benchmarking.
attributes.references: SRA Indemnity Insurance Rules; IFRS 17 Insurance Contracts; ABA Risk Management Guidelines

attributes.name: settlement_date
attributes.description: The date on which the claim arising from this exposure was formally settled or resolved. Populated when exposure_status transitions to 'closed'. Used for claims lifecycle analytics and PI insurance renewal reporting.
attributes.references: SRA Indemnity Insurance Rules; ABA Risk Management Guidelines

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: Identifies the operational system of record from which this exposure record originated or was ingested into the Silver Layer. Supports data lineage, reconciliation, and audit requirements.
attributes.references: ISO 27001 Information Security Management; Elite 3E Practice Management; Intapp Conflicts

attributes.name: to_register
attributes.description: FK to risk.risk_register.risk_register_id — PI exposure records represent specific risk items that should link back to the risk register for consolidated risk reporting.

attributes.name: to_risk_register
attributes.description: FK to risk.risk_register.risk_register_id — PI exposure records should link to the risk register item they represent. This connects the financial exposure tracking to the broader risk management framework.

products.name: pi_claim
products.description: Professional indemnity (PI) claim record capturing formal claims made against the firm by clients or third parties. Records claimant details, claim date, matter reference, alleged breach description, claim amount, insurer reference, coverage confirmation, legal representation assigned, settlement amount, claim outcome, and closure date. Managed in coordination with the firm's PI insurer and external coverage counsel.

attributes.name: pi_claim_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the professional indemnity claim record. Primary key for the pi_claim data product in the risk domain.

attributes.name: category_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to risk.risk_category. Business justification: PI claims are categorized by risk type. pi_claim has breach_category (STRING) which should normalize to risk_category for taxonomy consistency.

attributes.name: escalation_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to risk.risk_escalation. Business justification: PI claims may trigger escalations to governance bodies for decision-making. Valid business relationship for claims governance.

attributes.name: invoice_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to billing.invoice. Business justification: PI claims frequently originate from billing issues (overbilling allegations, rate disputes, guideline violations). Firms track which invoice(s) triggered the claim for defense preparation, settlement

attributes.name: matter_id
attributes.description: Reference to the underlying client matter from which the professional indemnity claim arises. Links the claim to the matter record in Elite 3E for context on the work performed, responsible timekeeper, and practice group.

attributes.name: primary_pi_attorney_profile_id
attributes.description: Reference to the external coverage counsel or internal attorney assigned to manage the firm's legal representation in the PI claim proceedings. Distinct from the responsible timekeeper on the underlying matter.
attributes.references: ABA Model Rules of Professional Conduct; Elite 3E Timekeeper Management

attributes.name: profile_id
attributes.description: Reference to the client entity associated with the matter giving rise to the claim. Enables linkage to the client domain for relationship history, KYC status, and conflict check records.
attributes.references: Elite 3E Client/Matter Management Module; Intapp Conflicts

attributes.name: register_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to risk.risk_register. Business justification: PI claims are materialized risks and should be tracked in the risk register. Valid business relationship for claims risk management.

attributes.name: responsible_timekeeper_id
attributes.description: Reference to the timekeeper (attorney or fee earner) identified as the responsible professional on the matter at the time the alleged breach occurred. Used for workforce risk analytics and PI exposure reporting.
attributes.references: Elite 3E Timekeeper Management; ABA Model Rules of Professional Conduct Rule 1.1

attributes.name: adr_method
attributes.description: The Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) method employed or proposed for resolving the PI claim outside of formal litigation. Null or 'none' if the claim is proceeding through court litigation or has been resolved without ADR.
attributes.references: ICC Arbitration Rules; LCIA Rules; ABA Model Rules of Professional Conduct; ADR principles

attributes.name: alleged_breach_date
attributes.description: The date on which the alleged act, error, or omission giving rise to the claim is said to have occurred. Relevant for determining the applicable policy period on a claims-made or occurrence basis and for limitation period analysis.
attributes.references: ABA Model Rules of Professional Conduct; Law Society of England and Wales

attributes.name: alleged_breach_description
attributes.description: Narrative description of the alleged act, error, or omission forming the basis of the professional indemnity claim. Includes the nature of the professional failing alleged (e.g., negligent advice, missed deadline, conflict of interest, breach of confidentiality). Protected by Legal Professional Privilege (LPP) considerations.
attributes.references: ABA Model Rules of Professional Conduct; SRA Standards and Regulations; LPP principles

attributes.name: claim_amount
attributes.description: The gross monetary amount claimed by the claimant against the firm, as stated in the formal claim notification or pleadings. Represents the claimant's quantification of alleged loss before any negotiation, mitigation, or settlement.
attributes.references: SRA Indemnity Insurance Rules; ABA Model Rules of Professional Conduct

attributes.name: claim_currency
attributes.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code in which the claim amount is denominated (e.g., USD, GBP, EUR). Required for multi-currency PI exposure reporting and insurer communication.

attributes.name: claim_date
attributes.description: The date on which the formal claim was made against the firm by the claimant or their legal representative. This is the principal business event date for the claim and determines the applicable policy year for PI insurance purposes.
attributes.references: SRA Indemnity Insurance Rules; Law Society of England and Wales PI Insurance Guidance

attributes.name: claim_outcome
attributes.description: The final resolution outcome of the professional indemnity claim. Populated upon closure of the claim. Used for risk analytics, insurer reporting, and lessons-learned reviews. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: settled|dismissed|judgment_for_claimant|judgment_for_firm|withdrawn|mediated|arbitrated — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: SRA Indemnity Insurance Rules; ABA Model Rules of Professional Conduct; ICC Arbitration Rules

attributes.name: claim_reference_number
attributes.description: Externally-known alphanumeric reference number assigned to the claim at inception, used in all correspondence with the PI insurer, coverage counsel, and claimant. Follows the firm's PI claim numbering convention (e.g., PI-2024-000123).
attributes.references: ABA Model Rules of Professional Conduct; SRA Indemnity Insurance Rules

attributes.name: claim_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the professional indemnity claim. Tracks progression from initial notification through investigation, insurer notification, litigation or negotiation, and final resolution. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: open|under_investigation|notified_to_insurer|in_litigation|settled|closed|withdrawn — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: SRA Indemnity Insurance Rules; ABA Model Rules of Professional Conduct

attributes.name: claimant_jurisdiction
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code representing the jurisdiction in which the claimant is domiciled or in which the claim is being pursued. Relevant for determining applicable law, limitation periods, and cross-border PI coverage.
attributes.references: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3; IBA Guidelines on Conflicts of Interest

attributes.name: claimant_name
attributes.description: Full legal name of the party making the professional indemnity claim against the firm. May be the firm's own client, a third party, or a counterparty to a transaction on which the firm advised. Classified confidential due to sensitivity of claim proceedings.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 4; DPA 2018; ABA Model Rules of Professional Conduct

attributes.name: claimant_type
attributes.description: Classification of the claimant's relationship to the firm. Distinguishes between the firm's own clients, third parties who relied on the firm's work product, counterparties to transactions, and regulatory bodies bringing disciplinary claims.
attributes.references: ABA Model Rules of Professional Conduct; SRA Standards and Regulations

attributes.name: closure_date
attributes.description: The date on which the professional indemnity claim was formally closed, whether by settlement, judgment, withdrawal, or other resolution. Null for open claims. Used to calculate claim duration and for portfolio run-off analysis.
attributes.references: SRA Indemnity Insurance Rules; ABA Model Rules of Professional Conduct

attributes.name: coverage_confirmed
attributes.description: Indicates whether the PI insurer has confirmed that the claim falls within the scope of the firm's professional indemnity policy coverage. True when coverage is confirmed; False when coverage is denied or under reservation of rights.
attributes.references: SRA Indemnity Insurance Rules; Law Society of England and Wales PI Insurance Guidance

attributes.name: coverage_denial_reason
attributes.description: Narrative explanation provided by the insurer for any denial of coverage or reservation of rights. Populated only when coverage_confirmed is False. Used for coverage dispute management and legal review.
attributes.references: SRA Indemnity Insurance Rules; Law Society of England and Wales PI Insurance Guidance

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp at which the PI claim record was first created in the risk data product. Represents the audit trail creation event, distinct from the claim_date (when the claim was made) and notification_date (when the insurer was notified).
attributes.references: ISO 27001; GDPR Article 5(1)(f); Internal Data Governance Standard

attributes.name: data_breach_reference
attributes.description: Cross-reference to the data breach incident record in the risk domain if the PI claim arises from or is associated with a data breach event. Enables linkage between the PI claims register and the data breach incident management register.

attributes.name: deductible_amount
attributes.description: The self-insured retention or deductible amount applicable to this claim under the firm's PI policy. Represents the portion of the claim cost borne directly by the firm before insurer indemnity applies.
attributes.references: SRA Indemnity Insurance Rules; Law Society of England and Wales PI Insurance Guidance

attributes.name: defence_costs_incurred
attributes.description: Cumulative legal and professional costs incurred by the firm in defending the PI claim, including external coverage counsel fees, expert witness fees, and court costs. Tracked separately from the settlement amount for insurer reimbursement and cost management purposes.
attributes.references: SRA Indemnity Insurance Rules; Elite 3E Financial Module

attributes.name: ethical_wall_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether an ethical wall (information barrier) has been established in Intapp Conflicts to prevent the timekeepers involved in the underlying matter from accessing PI claim information, protecting privilege and avoiding further conflict exposure.
attributes.references: Intapp Conflicts Ethical Walls Module; ABA Model Rules of Professional Conduct Rule 1.10; SRA Standards and Regulations

attributes.name: insurer_claim_reference
attributes.description: The reference number assigned to the claim by the PI insurer for tracking within the insurer's own claims management system. Used in all insurer correspondence and for reconciliation between the firm's records and the insurer's records.
attributes.references: SRA Indemnity Insurance Rules; Law Society of England and Wales PI Insurance Guidance

attributes.name: insurer_name
attributes.description: The name of the professional indemnity insurer or lead underwriter handling the claim. Required for insurer correspondence, coverage confirmation, and claims management coordination.
attributes.references: SRA Indemnity Insurance Rules; Law Society of England and Wales PI Insurance Guidance

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp at which the PI claim record was most recently modified. Used for audit trail, data lineage, and incremental load processing in the Databricks Silver Layer.
attributes.references: ISO 27001; GDPR Article 5(1)(f); Internal Data Governance Standard

attributes.name: limitation_expiry_date
attributes.description: The date on which the applicable limitation period for the claimant's cause of action expires. Critical for assessing whether the claim is time-barred and for managing the firm's procedural response deadlines.
attributes.references: Limitation Act 1980 (UK); applicable state statutes of limitations; ABA Model Rules of Professional Conduct

attributes.name: lpp_applies

attributes.name: notification_date

attributes.name: pii_data_involved

attributes.name: policy_number
attributes.description: The policy number of the professional indemnity insurance policy under which the claim is being notified and managed. Identifies the specific policy year and coverage layer applicable to the claim.

attributes.name: policy_year
attributes.description: The four-digit calendar year of the PI insurance policy period under which the claim is notified (e.g., 2024). Determines the applicable coverage limits, deductibles, and insurer for claims-made policies.

attributes.name: regulatory_report_date

attributes.name: regulatory_report_required

attributes.name: reserve_amount
attributes.description: The financial reserve established by the firm and/or its PI insurer to cover the estimated ultimate cost of the claim, including potential settlement, defence costs, and associated expenses. Used for financial provisioning and insurer reporting.

attributes.name: settlement_amount
attributes.description: The agreed monetary amount paid to the claimant to resolve the professional indemnity claim, as recorded upon settlement. Null if the claim has not been settled. Distinct from the original claim amount and the reserve.

attributes.name: settlement_date
attributes.description: The date on which the settlement agreement was executed and the claim was formally resolved by payment or other agreed consideration. Null if the claim has not been settled.

products.name: data_breach_incident

products.name: cyber_risk_event
products.description: Unified operational and cybersecurity risk event record serving as the single source of truth for all realized risk losses, near-miss events, and security incidents across the firm. Covers the full spectrum of operational risk events including process failures, system outages, human error, external events, as well as cybersecurity-specific events such as phishing, ransomware, DDoS, insider threats, and vulnerability exploits. Each record captures event date, event type and category, severity classification (aligned to ISO 27001 impact levels), affected systems or practice groups, detection source, containment actions, root cause analysis, financial impact (actual loss or near-miss estimated loss), matter reference if applicable, lessons-learned documentation, and linkage to ISO 27001 controls. Distinct from data_breach_incident which tracks privacy-specific regulatory notification obligations under GDPR Article 33/34.
